jobs.title: Lab Technician – Phlebotomist
jobs.description:
**Role Summary**
----------------

We are seeking a compassionate, detail-oriented, and dependable **Lab Technician / Phlebotomist** to support laboratory operations within an inpatient healthcare setting in Austin, Texas!

This is an excellent opportunity for a laboratory professional who enjoys providing hands-on patient care, performing accurate specimen collection, and contributing to essential healthcare services.

In this role, you will perform blood draws, collect and process specimens, maintain accurate documentation, and follow established laboratory standards and safety procedures.

You will work with a diverse patient population, including individuals receiving treatment for mental health conditions, intellectual or developmental disabilities, chemical dependency, and other behavioral or physical health conditions.

The ideal candidate is professional, compassionate, attentive to detail, and comfortable working with patients who have varying healthcare needs.

**Duties & Responsibilities**
-----------------------------

**Phlebotomy & Specimen Collection**

* Perform blood draws and specimen collection in accordance with established clinical and laboratory procedures.
* Properly identify patients before specimen collection.
* Accurately label, handle, prepare, and process laboratory specimens.
* Follow infection-prevention, safety, and quality-control standards.
* Maintain accurate documentation related to specimen collection and laboratory services.

**Patient Care & Communication**

* Interact professionally and compassionately with patients receiving inpatient habilitation or rehabilitation services.
* Work effectively with individuals experiencing mental health conditions, intellectual or developmental disabilities, chemical dependency, social challenges, and/or physical disorders.
* Maintain professionalism, confidentiality, and compassion when working with a diverse patient population.
* Protect patient confidentiality and comply with applicable patient privacy requirements.

**Laboratory Safety & Compliance**

* Follow all facility policies, procedures, attendance requirements, and safety protocols.
* Perform all duties in accordance with applicable rules and regulations governing laboratory technicians and phlebotomy services in the State of Texas.
* Follow applicable laboratory standards and facility requirements.
* Perform additional duties as assigned.

**Required Qualifications**
---------------------------

**Professional Qualifications**

* Qualified to perform phlebotomy and laboratory-related duties within the State of Texas.
* Ability to work effectively with patients in an inpatient behavioral health or rehabilitation environment.
* Strong attention to detail and ability to accurately follow specimen collection and handling procedures.
* Excellent interpersonal and communication skills.
* Ability to maintain professionalism, confidentiality, and compassion when working with a diverse patient population.

**Onboarding & Compliance**

* Must successfully complete all required onboarding, background, health, and facility clearance requirements before starting.

**Schedule & Training Availability**

* Must be available for the regular work schedule of **7:00 AM – 1:00 PM**.
* Must be available for **two non-consecutive training days**, specifically:

  + **Day 1:** 8:00 AM – 5:00 PM
  + **Day 6:** 8:00 AM – 5:00 PM
* Additional training may be completed during the regular work schedule.

**Desired Qualifications**
--------------------------

* **One year of blood-draw/phlebotomy experience preferred.**

**Why Consider This Opportunity?**
----------------------------------

* **Competitive Compensation:** Earn up to $41 per hour.
* **Potential Contract Extension:** Minimum six-month assignment, with possible extension based on performance and business needs.
* **Consistent Daily Schedule:** Regular working hours from 7:00 AM to 1:00 PM.
* **Meaningful Patient Care:** Support individuals receiving inpatient behavioral health, habilitation, and rehabilitation services.
* **Hands-On Laboratory Experience:** Apply your phlebotomy and specimen collection skills in a healthcare environment.
* **Professional Impact:** Contribute to accurate laboratory services and quality patient care.

**Location, Schedule & Work Type**
----------------------------------

**Job Title:** Lab Technician – Phlebotomist  
**Location:** Austin, Texas  
**Department:** Laboratory  
**Work Setting:** Inpatient Healthcare | Behavioral Health & Rehabilitation  
**Work Arrangement:** On-Site  
**Employment Type:** Contract  
**Contract Duration:** Minimum 6 Months, with Potential Extension Based on Performance and Business Needs  
**Regular Schedule:** 7:00 AM – 1:00 PM  
**Required Training:** Day 1 and Day 6 | 8:00 AM – 5:00 PM  
**Experience:** One Year of Blood-Draw/Phlebotomy Experience Preferred  
**State Requirement:** Must Be Qualified to Perform Phlebotomy and Laboratory-Related Duties in Texas

**If you're interested, please reply to this advertisement or directly email your resume to me at DSalgado@teemagroup.com or by calling/texting (949) 295-5951. I strive to reply within 48 hours. Looking forward to connecting with you soon.**

----------------

* Monitoring, controlling, or maintaining the quality of products or services in quality assurance, procurement, inspection, and production; OR

* Reviewing written quality or inspection procedures for adequacy and evaluating the implementation and effectiveness of quality/inspection systems, including sampling plans; OR
* Analyzing quality data to detect unsatisfactory trends or weaknesses in the quality/inspection system; OR
* Verifying by test or inspection, using sampling inspection or intensive product inspection techniques, that products comply with requirements prior to acceptance; OR
* Identifying inadequacies and requesting corrective action; OR
* Computing data, summarizing results, and preparing reports or charts depicting pertinent relationships using statistical methods; OR
* Investigating customer complaints and deficiency reports, and providing identification of causes to appropriate authorities; OR
* Reading, interpreting, and applying technical data such as blueprints, engineering drawings, product specifications, or technical manuals; OR

jobs.title: Analytical Chemist
jobs.description:
At Pattern Bioscience, we're tackling antibiotic resistance, one of the biggest public health challenges of our time. We use machine learning and microfluidics to quickly recognize the bacteria causing an infection and to predict which drugs will cure the infection.

We are hiring an Analytical Chemist to join our Consumable Manufacturing team during a critical inflection point in our company journey. We are actively investing in scaling our consumable production while developing the next assays for our platform. Your work will be key in ensuring precision in and quality of our reagent formulations for both current and future assays. Through your work, you will have the opportunity to work with research and process scientists, reagent manufacturing associates, and quality and automation engineers.

#### **Three Month Goals**

* Support development and validation of analytical methods for new assay panel research and development
* Independently manage routine HPLC qualification of manufacturing materials
* Independently manage inventory of reference materials and check standards to support HPLC program

#### **How You Will Contribute**

* Develop, optimize, and validate HPLC methods used for raw material, in-process, and finished reagent testing.
* Perform routine and non-routine HPLC and other analytical instrumentation testing (pH, conductivity, UV-Vis, refractometry, FTIR, NMR etc) to support batch release, stability studies, and process/manufacturing support.
* Following released procedures, formulate analytical standards for use in HPLC analysis.
* Troubleshoot chromatographic and instrument issues (columns, mobile phases, detectors, autosamplers, pumps) to minimize downtime and maintain lab operations.
* Author, review, and revise analytical test methods, SOPs, and work instructions; support the creation and execution of method validation protocols and reports.
* Support method transfer, method development, and equipment/test method validation activities for new and existing products.
* Analyze and interpret analytical data, including trending and statistical process control (SPC), to monitor equipment, method, and process performance over time.
* Investigate out-of-specification (OOS) and out-of-trend (OOT) results and atypical events; support nonconformance root cause analysis and CAPAs.
* Maintain, calibrate, and qualify analytical equipment systems and associated laboratory instrumentation; coordinate preventive maintenance and service with vendors.
* Partner with R&D, Manufacturing, and Quality teams to define material specifications, test methods, and acceptance criteria for reagents and raw materials.
* Maintain compliance with Good Documentation Practices, data integrity principles, and 21 CFR Part 11 requirements for all laboratory records and electronic data.
* Provide training and oversight to laboratory personnel on analytical methods, instrument operation, and data review.
* Support internal and external audits and regulatory inspections related to analytical testing.
* Are a thorough and relentless problem-solver, pursuing issues to their root cause.
* Keep the big picture in mind, knowing what needs to happen today to enable projects for later in the week, engaging subject matter experts or other teams as needed.
* Stay calm, adaptable, and flexible under changing priorities and the introduction of new methods.
* Excel in data analysis, particularly for chromatography data.
* Communicate clearly and efficiently in both oral and written formats, including technical writing and GxP documentation.

#### **Desired Education and Experience**

* B.S. in Chemistry, Biochemistry, Chemical Engineering, or a related scientific field.
* Min 2 years of hands-on HPLC and/or analytical chemistry laboratory experience, preferably within a regulated (GxP, FDA, or ISO 13485) environment.
* Demonstrated hands-on experience in analytical method development, qualification, validation, routine operation and troubleshooting.
* Working knowledge of complementary analytical techniques (e.g., UV-Vis/spectrophotometry, NMR, FTIR) is a plus.
* A strong understanding of FDA regulations and ISO 13485 requirements for IVD medical device development and production.
* Proficiency with chromatography data systems (e.g., Empower, Chromeleon, or similar CDS software).
* Understanding of cleanroom operations, BSL2 protocols, Good Documentation Practice, and GxP data integrity requirements.

**Details**

This is an exempt, salaried, full-time position on our Consumable Manufacturing team.

Join us! We're excited for what you can bring to our team. Here are a few things we provide to make sure you have a great experience. Learn more about our team by visiting our website.

**Benefits**

* Health insurance
* 401k Matching
* Paid Time Off
* The opportunity to make a global impact

To fulfill our mission and build world-changing technology, we've put together a diverse, multi-disciplinary top-notch team, a culture of innovation, learning, adaptability, and excellence and environment where people love coming to work.

We value diversity on our teams. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, religion, color, national origin, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, age, status as a qualified individual with disability, protected veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by law.

jobs.title: Phlebotomist-Lab Technician
jobs.description:

jobs.title: Quality Assurance Technician
jobs.description:
**Essential Functions**

A Ziegenfelder Quality Technician is responsible for:

* Ensuring that finished Ziegenfelder treats are ready for packaging by properly preparing raw material inputs, monitoring production processes, and inspecting final products to ensure customer satisfaction.
* Reviewing and documenting quality assurance processes and making recommendations for improvements.
* Manipulate a variety of stainless-steel hard pipes and flexible hosing to perform CIPs and batch processing.
* Participate in plant sanitation activities including floor scrubbing, drain cleaning, and other manual sanitation tasks.
* Participate in environmental monitoring program by collecting samples of finished product, work in progress, on equipment and around facility.
* Review and record microbiological data and report concerns and findings to Quality Manager.
* Use HMI to appropriately call ingredients for bulk processing and transfer of batches.
* Conducting production support to include mix making, equipment cleaning, product quality testing/sampling, and completion of the master sanitation schedule tasks.
* Verifying finished product meets quality standards of color, taste, quantity, wrap, and Rainbow Array.
* Adhering to HACCP, GMP, SOP, and SSOP programs and coordinating all documentation to ensure compliance with all federal, state, local, and Ziegenfelder directives, policies, and procedures.
* Perform chemistry testing to ensure product specifications.
* Troubleshoot equipment malfunctions and work cross-functionally with Production and Maintenance departments.
* Perform multiple quality checks and records results in the data control system as well as document batch records.
* Complete internal lab functions including environmental sampling and document completion.
* Conducting regular audits of documentation to ensure compliance with applicable federal, state, local, and Ziegenfelder directives, policies, and procedures.

Qualifications and Education Requirements

* One plus years within a food manufacturing facility, preferred.
* Preference will be given to Food Science, Food Technology Degree, or other related fields, however not required, experience will be considered.
* Experience and training with Food Safety, HACCP, SQF, Sanitation (SSOP & GMP) and/or other food safety systems and Quality Assurance process improvement skills required. SQF certification preferred but not required.
* Strong computer skills to include the use of Microsoft Office products.
* Excellent written and verbal communication skills.

**Physical Abilities**

* Standing up to 12 hours per day.
* Moving and lifting objects weighing up to 50 lbs. regularly, daily.
* Bending, twisting, reaching and grasping actions.
* Good spatial awareness working around manufacturing equipment.

**Working Conditions**

* Subject to cold temperatures of less than 32F for more than one hour with proper protection equipment.
* May be subject to noise above 85 decibels with proper protection equipment

**Compensation & Benefits**

* **Starting Pay:** $18.75/hour
* **Schedule:** 40 hours per week with set days off
* **Benefits:** Begin on the first day after 60 days of employment
* **401(k) with company matching**
* **Employee discounts**
* **Paid holidays**

**Who We Are**

The Ziegenfelder Company is part of the **Armstrong Group**, a family-owned organization founded in 1946. With over 2,400 employees nationwide, our brands span multiple industries including utilities, protection services, development, and frozen novelties.

At Ziegenfelder, we specialize in producing high-quality frozen twin pops under the **Budget Saver** brand, as well as private label products for major retailers like Walmart, Kroger, and Dollar General. Our facilities are located in Wheeling, WV; Chino, CA; Denver, CO; and Lockhart, TX.

We value **integrity, creativity, and innovation**, and are committed to positively impacting our workforce and the communities we serve.

**Armstrong is an Equal Opportunity Employer.**

**Who We Are**  
The Armstrong Group is a family owned and operated collection of diverse companies. What began in 1946 as Armstrong County Line Construction, founded by Jud L. Sedwick in Kittanning, PA, has now grown into an organization that encompasses multiple industries and employs over 2,400 individuals nationwide. Our brands include Armstrong Utilities, Guardian Protection, Armstrong Development, 4Front Solutions, Twin Pops, and Armstrong Comfort Solutions.
  
  
Armstrong is an Equal Opportunity Employer.

jobs.description:
At Fluor, we are proud to design and build projects and careers. If this sounds like a culture you would like to work in, you’re invited to apply for this role.

-------------------

• Review and become familiar with the project technical requirements such as the prime contract, applicable codes, standards, and specifications

• Monitor/inspect project and construction execution by regular surveillance and/or inspection as directed by the Site Quality Manager or supervisor to ensure that they comply with project requirements. Issue surveillance or inspection reports to appropriate parties and follow up until closure as required.

We are an equal opportunity employer. jobs.title: Water Resources Planner / Scientist
jobs.description:
About Us

We are an award-winning California-based environmental consulting firm with 600+ professionals and more than 30 years of diverse experience serving clients in transportation, energy, water, infrastructure, private development, and government sectors. Our mission is to deliver practical, science-based environmental and planning solutions that support communities, infrastructure, and natural systems. 

As a people-centric organization, we value collaboration, fairness, and transparency, and are committed to fostering a workplace that supports both personal and professional growth while offering robust career opportunities. We are especially proud of our recent Great Place To Work®
certification, which reflects an independent assessment of our culture and our team-member experiences.  

About The Role 

Rincon is seeking a Water Resources Planner/Scientist
with a background in California water supply/reliability, Sustainable Groundwater Management Act (SGMA), geology, hydrology, or hydrogeology to support our growing groundwater and water resources practice across California. This role will focus primarily on SGMA planning and implementation, watershed resilience planning, nature-based and groundwater recharge solutions, water resources planning, and grant funding strategies that move water resource solutions from planning toward implementation. Working with Project Managers, Principals-in-Charge, and interdisciplinary technical teams, you will conduct technical research and analysis; analyze groundwater, hydrologic, water quality, and other water resource data; and contribute to technical reports, planning documents, and funding applications. You will also work with public agency clients and interested parties throughout the planning process, helping to gather and evaluate data, support technical analyses, and communicate findings and recommendations. You will have opportunities to build the technical experience needed for greater responsibility and professional growth. 

You will interact with public agency clients, contribute to community outreach and engagement, and help strengthen client relationships through high-quality project delivery. 

We are looking for a motivated, curious, and collaborative professional who is eager to learn and make a tangible impact. This is an opportunity to build technical expertise, work alongside experienced water resources professionals, and help shape the next generation of sustainable and resilient water management across California. 

How We Collaborate 

This role may offer a hybrid work setup, blending time in the office with remote work as business needs evolve. We enjoy coming together in person to collaborate, connect with teammates, and partner with clients, and may prioritize candidates who live within 50 miles of a Rincon office.  
Eligible office locations for this role include Carlsbad, Fresno, Los Angeles, Monterey, Oakland, Palm Springs, Riverside, Sacramento, San Luis Obispo, San Diego, San Jose, Santa Barbara, and Ventura.  

What You’ll Do 

Support SGMA planning and implementation, including Groundwater Sustainability Plans and Alternatives, annual reports, periodic evaluations, plan updates, groundwater monitoring and data analysis, and evaluation of projects and management actions.  
Contribute to watershed resilience and climate adaptation planning by evaluating groundwater and surface water conditions, hydrology, water supply reliability, drought and climate impacts, and opportunities to improve long-term watershed resilience.  
Evaluate nature-based and groundwater sustainability solutions, including managed aquifer recharge, groundwater recharge, habitat and watershed restoration, stormwater capture, and green infrastructure, using geologic, hydrologic, hydrogeologic, and other technical information.  
Support grant applications and funding strategies for groundwater sustainability, recharge, watershed resilience, water supply, recycled water, wastewater, stormwater, and other water resource projects, including evaluating project benefits, readiness, and alignment with funding opportunities.  
Contribute to complex water resources planning documents, including Urban Water Management Plans, Water Shortage Contingency Plans, water supply and recycled water feasibility studies, watershed management plans, technical memoranda, and permitting and funding applications for water/wastewater facilities. 
Conduct technical research, field investigations, and analysis of groundwater, surface water, water supply, water quality, and related geologic and hydrologic conditions to support water resource planning, permitting, and project implementation.  
Prepare materials to support community and governing body engagement related to water resources projects, including drafting e-blasts, social media posts, presentations, resolutions and staff reports, posters, interview/input questions, surveys, and summaries of engagement efforts.   
Analyze and interpret technical data, including groundwater levels, water quality, water use, hydrologic conditions, and other datasets, and translate findings into clear, client-ready technical conclusions and recommendations.  
Prepare technical memoranda, reports, planning documents, presentations, and other materials for public agency clients and interested parties.  
Work collaboratively with hydrogeologists, geologists, engineers, planners, biologists, and other technical specialists and support client and stakeholder meetings, outreach, and project delivery. 

What You’ll Bring 

Bachelor’s degree in Geology, Hydrogeology, Hydrology, Water Resources, Environmental Engineering, Environmental Science, or a related technical field.  
Two or more years of relevant professional experience in groundwater, water resources, watershed management, hydrology, environmental planning, or a related field with an emphasis on SGMA and watershed resiliency.  
Foundational understanding of California water resources and interest in groundwater sustainability, water supply/reliability, watershed management, or climate resilience.  
Experience collecting, organizing, analyzing, and interpreting technical or environmental data.  
Strong technical writing and communication skills, with the ability to clearly communicate technical information to a variety of audiences.  
Ability to work collaboratively across technical disciplines, stay organized, and manage multiple assignments and priorities.  
Willingness to learn new technical tools, methods, and regulatory frameworks.  
Intermediate to advanced proficiency in Microsoft Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook, Teams, and other Microsoft products.  
Valid driver’s license with a clean driving record and willingness to conduct fieldwork and travel as project needs require. 

Nice to Have
Masters degree, coursework, or professional experience in geology, hydrogeology, hydrology, groundwater science, or another water-focused technical discipline.  
Experience with or interest in SGMA implementation, including Groundwater Sustainability Plans, annual reports, periodic evaluations, groundwater monitoring, or implementation of groundwater projects and management actions.  
Experience with groundwater or surface water monitoring, inter-connected surface water studies, groundwater dependent ecosystems, hydrologic analysis, water quality, managed aquifer recharge, groundwater-surface water interactions, or watershed assessment.  
Familiarity with California water laws, regulations, and programs, particularly SGMA and water rights.  
Experience with GIS, groundwater or hydrologic datasets, databases, modeling tools, or other technical analytical applications.  
Experience supporting grant applications, funding strategies, or implementation of groundwater, watershed, climate resilience, or water infrastructure projects.  
Professional certification or licensure, such as Professional Geologist (PG) license, Geologist-in-Training (GIT), Professional Engineer (PE), Engineer-in-Training (EIT) certification, or other relevant professional credential, or interest in pursuing professional licensure. 

Investing in You 

The base salary range for this full-time position is $70,000-$95,000
, plus a generous benefits program. Salary ranges are based on the market median of similar jobs, according to third-party salary benchmark surveys. Base pay is determined based on internal equity and a candidate’s job-related knowledge, skills, and experience. 

We offer a comprehensive Total Rewards Package designed to support employee well-being, growth, and financial security. Our benefits are designed to offer flexibility and choice, including health coverage options, employer-sponsored insurance, retirement benefits, generous time off, and programs that support learning, growth, and community engagement. 

Explore more about our culture, benefits, and life at Rincon on our Culture and Benefits page. 

Additional Employment Information 

Individuals offered employment must successfully complete a pre-employment drug screening as a condition of employment. Additionally, those hired who may be assigned to federal projects will be subject to further drug testing, including screening for cannabinoids (THC/marijuana), in compliance with the Drug-Free Workplace Act of 1988 and other applicable federal regulations, which take precedence over California state and local laws.

Lead or support watershed resilience and climate adaptation efforts, integrating groundwater, surface water, water supply, land use, climate vulnerability, and other technical information to develop practical long-term resilience strategies.

HAZWOPER 40-hour training.

Office work environment.

An exciting career awaits you

At MPC, we’re committed to being a great place to work – one that welcomes new ideas, encourages diverse perspectives, develops our people, and fosters a collaborative team environment.

The Logistics & Storage Environmental, Safety, Security and Product Quality (L&S ESS&PQ) department is seeking an enthusiastic, collaborative professional ready to expand their technical expertise, influence business decisions, and grow as an environmental leader. We are looking for candidates who build strong partnerships across teams, communicate effectively in both speaking and writing, and thrive in a fast-paced environment where their work can make a visible impact.

Position Summary:

The MPLX L&S ESS&PQ Group has a full-time, exempt opening for an Air Subject Matter Expert (SME) on the Air Compliance and Technical Support Team. This highly visible role will lead environmental air permitting and air compliance efforts for terminals, pipeline and marine facilities, and transport fleets across the country. The position offers an opportunity to shape compliance strategy, guide complex projects, build broad organizational relationships, and develop leadership capabilities while becoming a trusted technical advisor to the business.

Candidate location is flexible and can be based at any L&S location. This position may require up to 25% travel with occasional overnight stays.

Key Responsibilities:

Serve as a key member of an experienced team of Air SMEs, with opportunities to lead initiatives, broaden technical expertise, and influence environmental strategy. Responsibilities will include the following:

Serving as a trusted advisor to field Environmental Specialists by providing day-to-day air permitting and regulatory compliance support.

Leading and supporting implementation of new and revised air regulations (i.e., 40 CFR Part 60 Subpart XXa and Part 63 Subparts R and BBBBBB).

Collaborating with, and providing support and backup for, other Air SMEs (e.g., storage tanks, CEMS, LDAR), creating opportunities to expand expertise across multiple programs.

Performing and documenting New Source Performance Standards (NSPS) determinations for terminal, pipeline, and marine projects.

Leading and supporting air permit and compliance audits, communicating insights to stakeholders, and driving continuous improvement through the internal auditing program.

Representing L&S in rule advocacy efforts through trade organizations, such as the International Liquid Terminals Association (ILTA), and helping shape practical regulatory outcomes.

Creating and improving guidance documents and compliance tools that establish consistent practices and enable effective decision-making across the organization.

Developing and delivering training to field Environmental Specialists on a wide range of air compliance and permitting topics, strengthening technical capability across the team.

Helping lead emerging technology evaluations and digital transformation initiatives, such as Next Gen Maintenance and the new Environmental Accounting & Tasking system.
Serve as Air Permitting Coordinator for the L&S organization — a visible leadership assignment that connects environmental expertise with engineering, operations, business development, and senior stakeholders.

Represent L&S Environmental in engineering, business development, and other project-related meetings, providing clear recommendations and helping teams navigate permitting and scope decisions.

Own and advance the air permit and project tracking program.

Set air permitting priorities and strategically align internal and external resources.

Identify the timeliest and most cost-effective permitting pathways to support project schedules and business objectives.

Provide clear, proactive project updates — including scope changes and permit timing — to stakeholders and leadership.

Lead or support development of air permit applications, complete detailed reviews of draft permits, and recommend solutions to complex permitting issues.

Build productive relationships with state agencies and Field Environmental Specialists to obtain permits that support business objectives.

Develop into a recognized Air Permitting SME for New Source Review (NSR), Title V (major), and non-Title V (minor) permitting, with a pathway to broader technical and organizational leadership.

jobs.title: Environmental Science Educator - Yosemite
jobs.description:
**Have you always wanted to work in a National Park? Are you a passionate, dedicated educator who is enthusiastic about working with youth? NatureBridge offers full-time educator positions with health benefits, housing, and paid time off. Apply today!**

**About the Position**

NatureBridge provides overnight environmental science education experiences for more than 30,000 students and their teachers every year in the world’s best classrooms: our National Parks. Our mission is to connect young people to the science and wonder of the natural world, igniting self-discovery, and inspiring stewardship of the planet. Through our programs, students explore the outdoors, connect with their peers, discover themselves and develop a lasting relationship with science and the environment around them.

**NatureBridge Educator Schedule -** **Video: What is it like to work at NatureBridge?**

Environmental Science Educator (ESE) schedule varies week-to-week. ESEs can expect to deliver environmental science and team-building programs from 9am - 4pm for 3-5 day programs Monday - Friday, with variability during schools’ arrival and departure days. ESEs also run evening programs 2-3 times a week from 6:30pm - 8:30pm. On a regular program day, the ESE receives up to 30 minutes of paid preparation time. ESEs attend regular meetings with other ESEs, and the education and operations teams to discuss program updates and collaborative feedback to the community workplace. In addition to educational responsibilities, ESEs help in other departments when needed or asked.

**Tasks and functions**

During Program:

* Lead multi-day, student-centered, experiential environmental science programs in outdoor settings.
* Facilitate inclusive, culturally relevant instruction that incorporates multiple perspectives and connects learning to students’ lives and communities.
* Engage students in scientific practices through hands-on investigations, while tailoring programming to meet the specific needs of each school group, align with teacher-defined outcomes, and reflect the NatureBridge Theory of Change.
* Follow NatureBridge risk management policies and procedures, and use sound judgment to make decisions and manage risk while managing students’ physical and emotional well-being when leading groups in outdoor settings. Administer and document first aid as necessary and appropriate, and document as required by NatureBridge.
* Foster a supportive, respectful learning environment and model responsible environmental behavior.
* Design and lead evening programs or assist guest presenters and partners, typically twice weekly following the field day.

Outside of Program:

* Serve as an educator on standby when scheduled.
* Assess and document student learning; contribute to program reflection, evaluation and improvement.
* Participate in staff meetings, training sessions, and program debriefs and complete all required paperwork in a timely fashion.
* Maintain gear and contribute to campus stewardship.
* Contribute to fundraising efforts by sharing stories from the field.

### **Job Description and Duties**

**Per CCR 249.3, this job control may be used to fill subsequent vacancies.**

  

Under the supervision of the Senior Environmental Scientist (Supervisory), the Environmental Scientist will conduct environmental health inspections on dairy farms and at milk processing and PRMP plants, gather scientific data, research and investigate food safety hazards, collect samples for regulatory surveillance, test pasteurization equipment for proper operation and food safety controls, and provide analytical expertise and reports on specific food safety parameters on dairy farms, milk processing plants, bulk milk haulers and other dairy food and PRMP facilities, including those associated with possible illegal sales of substandard dairy products to California consumers.

  

As an employee of the California Department of Food & Agriculture (CDFA), you are required to perform the “essential functions” of the job, with or without reasonable accommodation. If you are interested in becoming part of a diverse and inclusive workforce where talent, experience, and expertise are valued, then CDFA is the place for you!!

  

This position is not eligible for visa sponsorship. Applicants must be authorized to work in the United States. The CDFA does not participate in E-Verify for employment authorization purposes.

You will find additional information about the job in the **Duty Statement**.

### **Working Conditions**

The duties of this job are performed outdoors approximately 75% of the time. The incumbent reports to the Regional Office only to pick up supplies, attend meetings and turn in required documents. Most of the workday will be spent traveling in a state vehicle to various locations throughout the region.

  

When working outdoors the incumbent may be exposed to extremes in temperature, fumes and gases. The noise level in equipment rooms may be high. The incumbent must follow CDFA, Division, and Branch employee health and safety policies, including but not limited to the Respiratory Protection Program.

  

This position may/may not be eligible for telework. The amount of telework is at the discretion of the CDFA and based on the current telework policy. The Mission of the California Department of Food and Agriculture (CDFA) is to safeguard a resilient food system and promote an equitable marketplace, cultivating a California grown food supply that is globally recognized for innovation, quality, and sustainability.

  

The Milk and Dairy Food Safety Branch (MDFS) is responsible for ensuring that milk, dairy products, and products resembling milk products (PRMPs) are safe, unadulterated, and properly labeled to safeguard public health. The Branch inspects dairy farms, bulk milk tanker trucks, and milk processing plants; issues permits and licenses to dairy farms and processing facilities; collects samples for regulatory testing to ensure compliance with food safety and quality standards; reviews product labels for conformance with regulations to avoid misleading information for consumers; completes in-depth reviews and food safety assessments of complex equipment or novel processing methods, and evaluates and licenses technical food safety competencies of dairy industry workers. The Branch also responds to food safety incidents, and initiates product impounds and recalls as warranted. Branch personnel provide training and supervision for county Approved Milk Inspection Services and conduct ratings and inspections of farms, processors, and manufacturers of single-service dairy containers for compliance with requirements of the United States Food and Drug Administration (FDA) to ensure approval of California dairy products in interstate commerce. In addition, the Branch ensures that commercial laboratory testing used to determine the basis of payment for milk or for screening of milk for drug residues prior to processing is conducted according to required methods to protect consumers and the marketplace.

Research Data Analyst 1 (5272C), Environmental Science, Policy, and Management #89414 About Berkeley
  
  
At the University of California, Berkeley , we are dedicated to fostering a community where everyone feels welcome and can thrive. Our culture of openness, freedom, and belonging makes it a special place for students, faculty, and staff, who are among the most talented and accomplished anywhere, including Nobel laureates, Pulitzer Prize winners, and MacArthur Fellows. Since our founding in 1868, we have been an engine for innovation - driving intellectual, economic, and social progress that benefits California, the U.S., and beyond. Together, we change the world.
  
  
At Berkeley, the best careers are built on a foundation of continuous learning and growth . We actively support professional development by providing all full-time staff employees with at least 80 hours of paid time per year and provide space for supportive colleague communities via numerous employee resource groups.
  
  
We invite applicants who are inspired by our Principles of Community and who are eager to be part of our exciting Strategic Plan , which charts Berkeley's next era of excellence.
  
  
Learn more about some of our accomplishments at Points of Pride .
  
  
Departmental Overview
  
  
The Department of Environmental Science, Policy, and Management is home to multidisciplinary research programs that recognize the urgency of the challenges-and the enormous opportunities-that may lead to transformative change. We have award-winning faculty in climate science, biodiversity, environmental policy, land use, and community outreach who are all driven by a collective interest in our environmental future.
  
  
Position Summary
  
  
The Coastal Climate Resilience Lab (PI Rachel Carlson) seeks a Research Data Analyst 1 in the area of remote sensing and geospatial analysis. This is a part-time position (20 hours per week).
  
  
The Research Data Analyst 1 will conduct data analysis supporting two ongoing research collaborations:
  
  
Remote sensing of freshwater plumes in California (PI Carlson and co-PIs Albert Ruhi and Kelly Hondula)
  
Effects of land use and land cover on nearshore marine environments (PI Carlson).
  
  
This position involves preparing and analyzing ecological datasets using established remote sensing and geospatial methods under the direct supervision of other researchers. The Research Data Analyst 1 will apply data science and quantitative modeling methods to map freshwater flux in the marine environment and evaluate interlocking patterns in human-dominated landscapes and benthic ecosystems. This position works in a team to coordinate data cleaning, quality control, and code documentation, complete computational analysis, and prepare data visualizations displaying analytical results for internal review.
  
  
The Research Data Analyst 1 would be based in the research laboratory of PI Dr. Rachel Carlson on the UC Berkeley campus. They would also be co-mentored by Dr. Albert Ruhi (co-PI, ESPM, Berkeley) and remotely by Dr. Kelly Hondula (Arizona State University). They would receive additional guidance from at least one PhD student. Remote working arrangements are considered.
  
  
The Research Data Analyst 1 would have the opportunity to participate in campus data science, wilderness first aid, and other professional development opportunities. They would have the opportunity to attend one USA-based conference each year. The PI's group provides a supportive work environment that recognizes and supports people of diverse identities and needs and prioritizes inclusive practices and field safety.
  
  
Application Review Date
  
  
The First Review Date for this job is October 26, 2026. For full consideration, please apply on or before the first review date.
  
  
Responsibilities
  
  
50%
  
  
Under direct supervision, performs basic statistical and data analysis.
  
Apply existing code to new data found from an online repository to deliver code outputs.
  
Apply an existing code script (existing method) to data on inputs to the California coastline.
  
Create reports and basic visualizations on results.
  
  
15%
  
  
Supports testing of research instruments and data sources.
  
Using standard geospatial software/tools and under direct supervision, create a map of tree species using an established method and protocol.
  
  
10%
  
  
Collects research data and prepares it for analysis.
  
  
10%
  
  
Assists with study design proposals and survey instruments.
  
  
5%
  
  
Assists with report preparation and / or analysis for internal constituents.
  
  
5%
  
  
Develops knowledge in areas of storage, documentation and dissemination of computerized data.
  
  
5%
  
  
Assists with evaluation and research of data reporting products.
  
  
Required Qualifications
  
  
Acquiring knowledge of research function. Acquiring ability to perform research analysis duties.
  
Acquiring statistical analysis, systems programming, and database design skills to perform research analysis duties.
  
Ability to effectively manage time and see assigned parts of projects through to completion on deadline.
  
Basic consultation and communication skills.
  
  
Education / Training
  
  
Bachelor's degree in related area and / or equivalent experience / training. (Required)

jobs.title: Environmental Health Specialist II
jobs.description:
About FACS

At FACS, our mission is to make environments safer and healthier for the people who live and work in them. As one of the nation's leading environmental health consulting firms, we help organizations protect their people, assets, and communities. We are built on purpose, partnership, and performance, delivering measurable impact with every client engagement.
Our Values

We live our mission through three core values:
People First:
Support our team and clients, promote professional growth, and value collaboration.
Integrity of the Science:
Deliver accurate, reliable results through objective, evidence-based practices.
Client Relationships for Life:
Build long-term partnerships and help clients address environmental health challenges.

Why Join Us

At FACS, you’ll contribute meaningful work that helps organizations protect their people, assets, and communities. You’ll join a collaborative, entrepreneurial, and mission-driven team that values scientific integrity, strong client relationships, and professional growth.
Ranked "Best Places to Work" for five consecutive years, we invest in your success through training, mentorship, and support for professional certifications, so you can grow, thrive, and build a career with lasting impact.
Curious to see what we do? Meet our team at FACS Experts.
About the Role

The Environmental Health Specialist II is a hands-on, field-based role supporting industrial hygiene, asbestos, and microbial (mold and moisture) projects. The Specialist performs on-site surveys, inspections, assessments, abatement oversight, air sampling, clearances, and project monitoring, and prepares clear, accurate written field reports.
This role may take the lead on assigned projects when Environmental Health Specialists or field technicians are assigned, coordinating closely with the Project Manager, contractors, and clients. Local travel to client and project sites is a regular part of the role.
Fieldwork and Reporting

Perform on-site surveys, inspections, assessments, abatement oversight, and monitoring for industrial hygiene, asbestos, and microbial projects.
Perform asbestos air sampling, clearances, and on-site analysis of air samples while adhering to quality-control requirements.
Prepare written field reports and maintain acceptable report turnaround times.
Identify and secure necessary tools and equipment for assigned projects.
Maintain internal QA/QC compliance.

Project Coordination and Communication

Take the lead on projects when Environmental Health Specialists or field technicians are assigned.
Communicate vital project information to Project Managers to support coordination and progress tracking.
Serve as a liaison between the client, Project Manager, and contractor.
Report project progress and provide technical input to the Project Manager.
Obtain and track project numbers for accurate record-keeping.
Adapt the scope of work in the field as needed to accommodate actual conditions or changes during project progression.

Compliance and Contractor Oversight

Review contractor personnel certifications, medical clearances, and other required documentation to ensure compliance with abatement requirements.
Act as a point of contact and meet with regulatory agents in the event of surprise site inspections.

Team Development and Professional Growth

Assist with training and mentoring junior staff.
Attend required internal and external technical training.
Maintain technical certifications.

Experience

Minimum of two years of experience as a field technician conducting field surveys, inspections, assessments, or asbestos-related monitoring work.
Proficiency with Microsoft Office, including Excel, and ability to quickly learn new software and systems.

Education and Credentials

Bachelor of Science in industrial hygiene, health and safety, biological science, physical science, or a related field—or equivalent relevant experience.
Current California Site Surveillance Technician (CSST) certification required.

Preferred Experience

Experience with asbestos abatement monitoring, air sampling, clearances, or indoor environmental quality work.
Experience serving as a field lead or coordinating with contractors, clients, or junior staff.

Physical & Work Requirements

Physical ability to stoop, kneel, climb, crawl, walk, and stand for extended periods in varied work environments while performing sampling activities
Ability to lift and carry equipment weighing up to 50 lbs.
Prolonged periods of sitting at a desk and working on a computer for documentation and reporting
Must be able to pass a background check, annual medical examinations, and OSHA-required respirator fit tests
Valid driver's license, reliable transportation, and current auto insurance
Ability to travel locally to assigned client and project sites

Compensation and Rewards

Competitive base salary with performance-based bonus structure tied to individual and team achievements
Comprehensive benefits package, including:
Medical coverage with 100% company-paid premiums for employees and their families, plus 50% of the annual deductible covered by the company
401(k) retirement plan with company matching contributions
Vision and dental plan options
Flexible Spending Accounts (health care and dependent care)
Company-sponsored programs including Employee Assistance Program, life and disability insurance, Rocket Lawyer legal services, and mobile phone plan with Verizon
Voluntary benefits options including supplemental life insurance for employees and dependents, short-term disability, hospital, accident, and pet insurance
Generous PTO (3 weeks accrual), paid holidays, volunteer days, and floating holiday
Tuition Reimbursement Program to promote higher education
Paid training and certifications to support career advancement
Incentive Bonus Plan and Donation Matching Program

Wage Transparency

Pay for this position is based on a number of factors including geographic location, relevant knowledge, skills, and experience.
Why Join FACS

If you are a certified CSST or experienced environmental health field professional who enjoys hands-on fieldwork, asbestos and microbial projects, and supporting clients and project teams, we encourage you to apply. This is an opportunity to take on field leadership, develop technically, and grow within a specialized environmental health consulting practice.
Equal Opportunity Employer

Forensic Analytical Consulting Services is an equal-opportunity employer that complies with EEOC rules and regulations. We are committed to diversity, equity, and inclusion and do not discriminate based on race, age, disability, or other non-merit characteristics. We welcome all candidates to apply, including women, people of color, persons with disabilities, and veterans.
Employment Contingency

Employment is contingent upon successful completion of background check and drug screening.

Gs-09

Understanding and following the principles of the Environmental Program by providing guidance and assistance to generator personnel, DLA Disposition Services personnel, and customer/contracted personnel in support of the mission requirements.

GS-11:

C. jobs.description:
Work with Us. Change the World.

At AECOM, we're delivering a better world. Whether improving your commute, keeping the lights on, providing access to clean water, or transforming skylines, our work helps people and communities thrive. We are the world's trusted infrastructure consulting firm, partnering with clients to solve the world’s most complex challenges and build legacies for future generations.

There has never been a better time to be at AECOM. With accelerating infrastructure investment worldwide, our services are in great demand. We invite you to bring your bold ideas and big dreams and become part of a global team of over 50,000 planners, designers, engineers, scientists, digital innovators, program and construction managers and other professionals delivering projects that create a positive and tangible impact around the world.

We're one global team driven by our common purpose to deliver a better world. Join us.

Job Description

AECOM is seeking an experienced Environmental Scientist III / Senior Environmental Scientist
to join our Environmental Remediation Practice in Richmond, California
.

The successful candidate will provide technical leadership and project coordination for environmental investigation, remediation, groundwater monitoring, compliance, and emergency response projects throughout Northern California and the western United States. This position will support a diverse portfolio of industrial, energy, transportation, municipal, and commercial clients while collaborating with multidisciplinary teams of scientists, engineers, geologists, and technical specialists.

The ideal candidate will have strong experience managing environmental field programs, coordinating subcontractors and laboratories, overseeing health and safety compliance, managing environmental data, and preparing technical and regulatory deliverables.

This position will be based in Richmond, California, with opportunities to support projects throughout Northern California and the western United States.

Responsibilities

Technical and Project Leadership

Lead environmental investigation, monitoring, remediation, and compliance projects from planning through execution.
Coordinate field schedules, staffing, subcontractors, laboratory services, equipment, and site logistics.
Develop and implement work plans, sampling plans, health and safety documentation, and project-specific field procedures.
Support project managers with project planning, budgeting, scheduling, resource forecasting, and client communications.
Identify project risks and develop solutions to achieve project objectives while maintaining quality, schedule, and budget commitments.

Groundwater Monitoring and Remediation

Plan and oversee groundwater, soil, sediment, and waste characterization programs.
Manage groundwater monitoring events and environmental sampling activities.
Coordinate remedial investigations, corrective action programs, groundwater treatment systems, and in-situ remediation efforts.
Evaluate environmental data and support development of remedial strategies and technical recommendations.
Ensure field activities are performed in accordance with project requirements and applicable regulations.

Environmental Compliance

Support environmental compliance programs for industrial, infrastructure, remediation, and construction projects.
Conduct environmental inspections, audits, and compliance assessments.
Monitor project activities for compliance with permits, mitigation measures, Environmental Protection Plans (EPPs), and Storm Water Pollution Prevention Plans (SWPPPs).
Coordinate with regulatory agencies, contractors, and stakeholders to support permitting and environmental compliance objectives.

Health and Safety

Implement and enforce site-specific Health and Safety Plans (HASPs), Job Safety Analyses (JSAs), and company safety procedures.
Lead daily safety meetings, hazard assessments, and pre-task planning activities.
Support atmospheric monitoring, radiological monitoring, confined-space activities, and other specialized health and safety requirements.
Promote a strong safety culture through leadership, mentoring, and continuous improvement.

Technical Reporting and Data Management

Prepare and review technical reports, groundwater monitoring reports, regulatory submittals, and field documentation.
Perform QA/QC reviews of environmental data, field records, and project deliverables.
Manage environmental databases and electronic reporting platforms, including EQuIS and GeoTracker.
Support data validation, interpretation, and presentation of technical findings to clients and regulatory agencies.

Team Development

Mentor and provide technical guidance to junior environmental professionals.
Coordinate multidisciplinary teams including environmental scientists, geologists, engineers, biologists, technicians, and subcontractors.
Support staff development through field training, technical mentoring, and knowledge sharing initiatives.

Qualifications

Minimum Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in Environmental Science, Geology, Biology, Environmental Engineering, Natural Resources, or a related field and 4+ years environmental consulting or related professional experience (groundwater monitoring, environmental sampling, remediation field activities, and environmental compliance programs, leading project teams, coordinating complex environmental projects, experience preparing technical reports and regulatory deliverables, etc.) or demonstrated equivalency of experience and/or education.
A valid driver’s license is required, along with the ability to pass a Motor Vehicle Records (MVR) check in accordance with company policy.
Employment is contingent upon successfully completing a pre-employment background check and drug screen.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience supporting California environmental remediation programs, including DTSC, RWQCB, and GeoTracker reporting requirements.
Experience at refinery, chemical, manufacturing, terminal, energy, or other industrial facilities, including CERCLA, RCRA, corrective action, and groundwater remediation programs.
Experience managing subcontractors, coordinating multidisciplinary project teams, and supporting emergency response and disaster recovery.
Experience with complex groundwater monitoring and reporting, environmental site investigations, remediation, compliance, and regulatory reporting.
Proficiency in EQuIS, GeoTracker, environmental database management, QA/QC, data validation, technical report preparation, SWPPP compliance, HASPs, JSAs, atmospheric and radiological monitoring.
Relevant training and certifications: current OSHA 40-Hour HAZWOPER, OSHA 8-Hour HAZWOPER Refresher, OSHA Site Supervisor Training, RCRA Hazardous Waste Management Training, Radiation Safety or Radiological Monitoring Training, Confined Space Entry Training, and First Aid/CPR Certification.

Additional Information

AECOM is unable to provide employment visa sponsorship now or in the future for this position.
Position may involve local and regional travel, field assignments, and periodic overnight travel.

To support this commitment, all newly hired employees are required to attend an in-person Day 1 onboarding at an AECOM office location as a condition of employment.

AECOM is proud to offer comprehensive benefits to meet the diverse needs of our employees. Depending on your employment status, AECOM benefits may include medical, dental, vision, life, AD&D, disability benefits, paid time off, leaves of absences, voluntary benefits, perks, flexible work options, well-being resources, employee assistance program, business travel insurance, service recognition awards, retirement savings plan, and employee stock purchase plan.

Our teams partner with public- and private-sector clients to create innovative, sustainable and resilient solutions throughout the project lifecycle – from advisory, planning, design and engineering to program and construction management. AECOM is a Fortune 500 firm that had revenue of $16.1 billion in fiscal year 2025. Learn more at aecom.com.

What Makes AECOM a Great Place To Work

Work on groundbreaking projects - both in your local community and on a global scale - that are transforming our industry and shaping the future. With cutting-edge technology and a network of experts, you’ll have the resources to make a real impact. Temp Senior Research Associate, Investigative Toxicology

Revolution Medicines is a clinical-stage precision oncology company focused on developing novel targeted therapies to inhibit frontier targets in RAS-addicted cancers. The company’s R&D pipeline comprises RAS(ON) Inhibitors designed to suppress diverse oncogenic variants of RAS proteins, and RAS Companion Inhibitors for use in combination treatment strategies. As a new member of the Revolution Medicines team, you will join other outstanding scientists in a tireless commitment to patients with cancers harboring mutations in the RAS signaling pathway.

The Opportunity:

We are seeking a highly motivated Senior Research Associate to support laboratory research activities focused on the development and execution of investigative toxicology (iTox) predictive assays and workflows to enable improved safety translation to the clinic. The ideal candidate will have a strong understanding of the technical needs in a lab as well as significant hands-on experience with standard/bespoke cell culture and in vitro cell biology techniques. Further, the successful candidate will:

Develop novel approach methods (NAMs) including predictive 2D/3D models for nonclinical safety assessments.
Independently perform experiments related to in vitro/ex vivo 2D/3D assays using lab techniques that include cell viability/cell death, flow cytometry, primary cell culture, animal sample processing, molecular and cell isolation, immunofluorescence, plate-based reporter assays and ELISA/Luminex
Support in vivo study design, data analysis, study coordination and sample management
Analyze, interpret and accurately document assay/study results in an electronic lab notebook or other technical reporting formats
Work independently and collaboratively in a team to ensure timely and accurate data analysis and communication to support decision-making and contribute to high-quality study reports.
Support the operation, maintenance, and troubleshooting of lab instruments and contribute to the evaluation and adoption of new technologies for enhanced toxicity prediction, compound screening, and development of translational safety biomarkers.
Manage day-to-day experimental/study related activities in the lab and work effectively with Contract Research Organizations (CROs), RevMed study operations, internal scientists and subject matter experts (SMEs).
Maintain a safe and organized lab environment and support development and/or review of protocols, SOPs, policies, and guidelines.

Required Skills, Experience, and Education:

Bachelor/Master’s degree in Pharmaceutical Sciences or a related scientific discipline, with 5+ of relevant industry experience or 3+ years of postgraduate working experience.
Hands-on experience in operating and maintaining cell culture and standard lab instruments.
Experience maintaining lab environment, lab infrastructure and sample management.
Experience with animal sample processing and advanced cell culture techniques for immortalized cell lines, primary cells (including PBMCs) and/or iPSC cells.
Cell and molecular biology methods, including flow cytometry, Luminex/MSD, ELISA, cell viability/death assays.
Ability to conduct multiple laboratory and project tasks efficiently.
Ability to work in a team-oriented environment with flexibility.
Highly organized, detail-oriented, excellent record-keeping skills, and being able to adapt to a dynamic and fast-paced environment.
Strong written and verbal communication skills, with a demonstrated ability to collaborate effectively in a team environment.

Preferred Skills:

Experience working with small molecules and targeted oncology therapeutics of all modalities.
Experience working in a matrixed team environment at a biotech/pharma company or CRO.
3D assays, data analytics/ in silico experience is a plus.

This is a contract position that will be employed through a third-party recruiting agency. The agency will provide the pay range, which will be based on several factors, including job-related skills, experience, market conditions, and relevant education or training.

Do you have a passion for protecting the environment and ensuring the sustainability of our natural resources? The Central Coast Water Board is seeking an experienced, knowledgeable, and motivated Environmental Scientist to join our team in San Luis Obispo, California. In this position, you will play a critical role as our region’s scientific expert on surface water quality issues with a focus on developing total maximum daily loads (TMDLs) and accompanying implementation plans to address the complex impacts of pesticides, nutrients, toxins, and other pollutants to water quality and human health.

The Environmental Scientist will focus on developing TMDL projects using new or emerging science for pesticides and associated toxicity, nutrients, biological indicators (e.g., bacteria indicators, harmful algal bloom species and associated algal toxins, benthic invertebrate species, bioaccumulation in sport fish and prey fish, etc.), and molecular detection of biological indicators. This position will study the toxicity of pollutants to assess their impact on water quality and aquatic ecosystems. The Environmental Scientist will also be tasked with reviewing peer-reviewed scientific research and designing novel approaches to develop numeric thresholds for pesticides, nutrients, and other toxic pollutants for TMDLs, planning documents, or other regulatory mechanisms that protect water quality. Applicants with particular interest in pesticides and pesticide-related-toxicity are strongly encouraged to apply.

The Environmental Scientist will also be responsible for supporting water quality data assessments that inform the federal Clean Water Act section 303(d) List and section 305(b) Report.

At the Central Coast Water Board, we're committed to protecting and improving the water quality in our region. Your work will be critical in helping us achieve our mission of preserving and protecting the natural resources in our region.

jobs.description:
Arcadis is the world's leading company delivering sustainable design, engineering, and consultancy solutions for natural and built assets.

We are more than 34,000 people, in over 30 countries, dedicated to improving quality of life. Everyone has an important role to play. With the power of many curious minds, together we can solve the world’s most complex challenges and deliver more impact together.

**Role description:**

Arcadis is currently searching for an Entry-Level Geologist to join our Resilience Environment team in Sacramento, CA. This position is slated to start in Summer 2027. Candidates who are graduating in May 2027 are encouraged to apply.

**Role accountabilities:**

As part of this role, you will be responsible for assisting Project Managers (PMs) and Task Managers (TMs) in planning and executing environmental site characterization, investigation, and remediation tasks.

Fieldwork will also be a key aspect of this position, which will offer you an opportunity to be trained to oversee drilling for soil sampling and groundwater well installation, groundwater sampling, subcontractor oversight, operation and maintenance of remediation systems, vapor intrusion/soil gas surveys, among other tasks. It is essential to conduct fieldwork with a focus on health and safety.

Your core duties will include:

* Prepare subcontracts and oversee the work of subcontractors.
* Writing and preparing technical reports, work plans, letters, and memoranda
* Office work may include task coordination, data compilation and interpretation, cost estimates, health & safety plan preparation, report writing, regulatory file reviews, proposal writing, project strategy development, schedule and budget management, and establishment of subcontracts.
* Conducting field work including soil, groundwater, and/or vapor sampling in the field. Field work will require regional business travel for up to 1-2 days per week on average. A few times per year, travel will be required within the U.S. for up to two weeks at a time.

To be successful in this role, you should possess strong written and oral communication skills, be self-motivated, and exhibit independent thinking. You should be able to work effectively and efficiently in a team setting as well as independently and remotely. Successful candidates will demonstrate their ability to be adaptable, creative problem solvers who can work collaboratively as a team member.

In summary, this position encompasses both office work (task management, data analysis, report preparation, scope preparation, and client communications) as well as field work.

Fieldwork will also be a key aspect of this position, which will offer you an opportunity to be trained to oversee drilling for soil sampling and groundwater well installation, groundwater sampling, subcontractor oversight, operation and maintenance of remediation systems, vapor intrusion/soil gas surveys, among other tasks.

Additionally, Arcadis supports many of our client’s needs when unforeseen incidents occur, such as train derailments, pipeline releases, etc. An aspect of this role is supporting our Pacific Northwest and National emergency response teams to ensure rapid protection of human health and the environment. This work is completed under the direction of trained incident responders and may require unanticipated travel and work outside standard business hours.

Field work will require regional business travel for up to 1-2 days per week on average. A few times per year, travel will be required within the U.S. for up to two weeks at a time. Estimated travel is up to 75% during the first two years, with travel reduced with career growth. By the third year, travel for field work is typically 50%. Travel expenses are reimbursable.

**Qualifications & Experience:**

**Required Qualifications**

* Bachelor’s of Science in Geology, Engineering, or closely related field (i.e., environmental, biological, physical science)

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Master of Science degree in Geology, Engineering or closely related field (i.e., environmental, biological, physical science)
* Current OSHA 40-hour HAZWOPER training

Why Arcadis?

We can only achieve our goals when everyone is empowered to be their best. We believe everyone's contribution matters. It’s why we are pioneering a skills-based approach, where you can harness your unique experience and expertise to carve your career path and maximize the impact we can make together.

You’ll do meaningful work, and no matter what role, you’ll be helping to deliver sustainable solutions for a more prosperous planet. Make your mark, on your career, your colleagues, your clients, your life and the world around you.

Together, we can create a lasting legacy.

Join Arcadis. Create a Legacy.

Our Commitment to Equality, Diversity, Inclusion & Belonging

We want you to be able to bring your best self to work every day. Our ambition is to be an employer of choice and provide a great place to work for all our people. We are an equal opportunity employer. We are dedicated to a policy of non-discrimination in employment on any basis including race, creed, color, religion, national origin, sex, age, disability, marital status, sexual orientation, gender identity, citizenship status, disability, veteran status, or any other basis prohibited by law.

Arcadis offers benefits for full time and part time positions. These benefits include medical, dental, and vision, EAP, 401K, STD, LTD, AD&D, life insurance, paid parental leave, reward & recognition program and optional benefits including wellbeing benefits, adoption assistance and tuition reimbursement. We offer nine paid holidays and 15 days PTO that accrue per year. The salary range for this position is $55,200- $82,800. Actual salaries will vary and are based on several factors, such as experience, education, budget, internal equity, project and location.

APTIM is seeking a motivated entry-level Environmental Scientist to support our portfolio of federal environmental investigation and remediation projects. Projects commonly involve the investigation and remediation of sites with groundwater or soil impacted by chlorinated solvents, petroleum, radiological contaminants, or emerging compounds. The successful candidate will work under the supervision of project managers and partner with other engineers, scientists, geologists, risk assessors, and health physicists.

**Key Responsibilities/Accountabilities:**

* Assist with the collection, documentation, and organization of field data to support project objectives.
* Contribute to the preparation of project work plans and deliverables.
* Assist with the development of technical scopes of work and cost estimates for proposal efforts.
* Develop and maintain spreadsheets, dashboards, and data-tracking tools.
* Assist in the management, analysis, and interpretation of environmental data using statistical analysis and data visualization tools.
* Identify and evaluate environmental risks and recommend remediation strategies to support compliance with federal, state, and local regulations.
* Adhere to established health and safety policies and procedures and execute work in a safe and conscientious manner.

**Basic Qualifications:**

* Bachelor's degree in environmental science or a related scientific discipline (completed or in progress).
* Relevant internship, research, or academic project experience involving environmental investigation, water or wastewater treatment, sustainability, or ecological conservation (0–2 years).
* Strong interest in environmental remediation, field investigations, treatment systems, and environmental compliance.
* Must have strong written and oral communication skills.
* Willingness to learn field sampling methods, equipment operation, and environmental data collection procedures.
* Ability to perform essential field duties, including walking on uneven terrain, lifting and carrying field equipment, and working outdoors in varying weather conditions.
* Ability to wear and use required PPE.
* Ability to travel to work sites, including overnight travel.
* Valid driver's license.
* Must be a U.S. citizen or authorized to work on federal contracts.

**Preferred Qualifications:**

* Completion of 40-hour OSHA HAZWOPER training.
* Experience using AI tools (e.g., Microsoft Copilot, ChatGPT, or similar tools) to support technical communication, analytical tasks, research, and efficient project execution. Upon hire, employees are expected to use these tools in accordance with approved company guidelines.

**About APTIM**

APTIM enhances the quality of the environment, wellbeing of people, resilience of communities, and opportunity for employees to make a difference, not just a living. A leading professional solutions firm, we specialize in environmental, sustainability, resilience, and infrastructure solutions. Our team of experts provide these integrated solutions for forward-thinking government agencies, commercial and industrial clients, and energy customers. Together, we create sustainable and resilient communities for all.

What you can expect from APTIM:

* Work that is worthy of your time and talent
* Respect and flexibility to live a full life at work and at home
* Dogged determination to deliver for our clients and communities
* A voice in making our company better
* Investment into your personal and professional development

As of the date of this posting, a good faith estimate of the current pay range for this position is $33.00 to $40.00 per hour Compensation depends on several factors including: experience, education, key skills, geographic location of the position, client requirements, external market competitiveness, and internal equity among other employees within APTIM.

**Employee Benefits**

APTIM Federal Services, llc is committed to providing an extensive range of benefits that protect and promote the health and financial well-being of our employees and their families through the APTIM Benefits Marketplace https://aptim.makeityoursource.com/.

* Medical, vision, and dental insurance: Through the marketplace, our employees can choose benefits from five metallic levels and several carriers to find the right benefits that work for them in their location.

**Company Description**

*“I've been with AECOM for over a decade, and when I reflect on why I stay with the company it is because of workplace culture and the nature of our projects. Working on impactful community-shaping projects with unique and diverse challenges, having opportunities for meaningful career progression, and being a part of a caring, close-knit team that supports each other through life's ups and downs.” –* ***Alix Chinnery, Associate Director - Environment, Perth, WA***

**Come grow with us.**

AECOM's environmental practice is dedicated to helping industries, clients and governments meet their environmental responsibilities while protecting the natural environment. We provide advisory and technical services to ensure compliance, manage impacts, and reduce risks, including obtaining permits and approvals, decommissioning and restoring contaminated sites, and tackling climate change challenges and resilience. We focus on preserving habitats, water quality, stakeholder engagement and cultural resources, promoting a holistic approach to environmental impact management at every project stage.

**Everyone belongs at AECOM.**

We’re committed to diversity, equity, inclusion, and belonging - because great ideas come from diverse perspectives. AECOM is proud to be a **Fortune 500 Most Admired Company**, a **WGEA Employer of Choice for Gender Equality**, #**Work180 Equitable Workplace Awards 2025 Winner** and an **AWEI Bronze Tier LGBTQ+ Inclusive Employer**.

 **Job Description**

We are looking for a passionate Graduate Environmental Planner / Scientist to join our **Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA)** teamin Newcastle.

At AECOM, our Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA) team is helping deliver some of the most transformational projects in Australia – from renewable energy and transmission projects, to major road, rail, water and industrial developments. We combine innovative technologies with decades of expertise to deliver robust, easy-to-understand analyses that achieve compliance, support clients’ Environmental, Social and Governance (ESG) objectives, and create meaningful change for communities.

**How you'll make a difference:**

* Apply your environmental science, planning, or engineering qualifications to real-world challenges.
* Work with multi-disciplinary teams of scientists, planners, engineers, drafters, project administrators and contractors in a fast-paced consulting environment.
* Develop skills in environmental assessment across renewable energy, water, and transport sectors, as well as in navigating approval pathways under Commonwealth, State, and local frameworks.
* Support ESG initiatives by engaging with communities and key stakeholders.
* Embed sustainability and resilience outcomes within projects.

You’ll have opportunities to collaborate across Australia, New Zealand and globally, with access to a strong pipeline of projects and a network of mentors to help you shape your career.

**What our Graduate Program offers:**

* **Graduate Introduction:** Kickstart connections with peers and leaders.
* **Essential Consulting Skills:** Master core consulting skills from day one.
* **Networking and Learning:** Grow your network and industry know-how.
* **Mentoring and Career Support:** Receive guidance from experienced professionals.
* **Learning from Experts:** Learn directly from industry leaders and specialists.
* **Flexible Work Options:** Work in a way that fits your life and wellbeing.
* **Career Pathways:** Get support to progress and step confidently into your next role.

For more information, visit our Early Careers website.

**Additional Information**
