* **Interview:** Attend a face-to-face interview at your local office.

*Applications are reviewed as they come in, and the role may close earlier than expected, so if this opportunity sounds like you, we encourage you to apply as soon as possible.*

**What sets us apart?**

We are the trusted global infrastructure leader.

Across the globe, we partner with our clients in the public and private sectors to solve their most complex challenges, pioneer innovative solutions and deliver a better world.

Our reputation is recognised globally. We are named the world’s top design firm and ranked #1 in Transportation, General Building, and Environmental Engineering by Engineering News-Record in 2025.

We are also honoured to be listed among Fortune’s “World’s Most Admired Companies” for the twelfth consecutive year and recognised as one of the 2025 World’s Most Ethical Companies by Ethisphere for our commitment to integrity and creating positive impact.

We welcome applications from individuals of all backgrounds, including those with disabilities, additional health or mental health needs, and/or neurodiverse conditions. If you require any adjustments during the hiring process, please let us know.

jobs.title: Associate Consultant, Air Quality
jobs.description:
**Company Description**

Applicants must be currently authorized to work in the United States on a full-time basis. No sponsorship is available for this position.

**Inviting bright minds**

Do you want to develop your excellence in an open, collaborative and creative culture? We work to create a sustainable future and our inspiring projects and innovative solutions aim to set the standard among our peers. You will join a global company that has been growing successfully since its founding in 1945. Together, we lead and leave a positive impact on societies, companies and people around the world.  
  
Ramboll is seeking an Air Quality Intern to join the firm’s offices in Los Angeles or Irvine, California, or Phoenix, Arizona in Spring/Summer 2027. If you are detail-oriented, self-motivated and enjoy thinking “outside-of-the-box,” please apply! If you can work in a team, apply analytical skills, and are looking to get your hands dirty (literally and figuratively), then you may find Ramboll to be an ideal place to start your career.

 **Job Description**

**You will join our Environment & Health** **department**

As our new Entry Level Air Quality Consultant you will be part of the Air & Climate Service Line within Ramboll’s Environment & Health Division. This group consists of like-minded individuals who are passionate about air and climate issues and assisting Ramboll’s clients with their most challenging problems. The Air & Climate team consults with clients across various industries on a range of topics, including but not limited to emissions estimation, air dispersion modeling, human health risk assessment, climate change, permitting, and compliance.

Your key tasks and responsibilities will be:

* + Preparing emissions calculations
  + Conducting air quality reviews of emissions reduction or control
  + Assisting in preparing major and minor source permit applications and environmental impact reports
  + Critically reviewing and interpreting local, state, and federal environmental regulations

  
**Qualifications**

**Your starting point for constant growth**

From the moment you join Ramboll, we will support your personal and professional development so that you grow with the company. For this role, we believe your starting point is:

* B.S. or M.S. in Chemical, Mechanical, Civil, or Environmental Engineering, Environmental Science, Atmospheric Science, or a science degree with air quality course work with a GPA of 3.5 or higher
* Strong computing skills including high level use of spreadsheets and word processing
* Strong written/verbal communication, problem-solving and organization skills
* Ability to understand and interpret environmental regulations
* Database and GIS skills are preferred but not required

  
**Additional Information**

**Welcome to our Environment & Health division**  
Ramboll develops innovative, scientifically sound solutions that help increase live ability by reducing pollution and restoring natural environments. One of the world’s leading environmental and health consultancies, our bright minds are trusted by clients to manage their most challenging environmental, health and social issues.

**Ramboll in the Americas**

Ramboll is a global architecture, engineering, and consultancy company. As a foundation-owned people company, founded in Denmark, we believe that the purpose of sustainable change is to create a thriving world for both nature and people. So, that’s where we start – and how we work. Our history is rooted in a clear vision of how a responsible company should act and being open and curious is a cornerstone of our culture. Ramboll in the Americas has thousands of experts working across more than 70 offices. Ramboll experts deliver innovative solutions across Environment & Health, Water, Energy, and Planning & Urban Design.

**Salary Transparency Statement**

At Ramboll, we are committed to fair and transparent compensation practices that support our people and our purpose of creating sustainable societies. The anticipated base salary range for this position is $64,404 to $80,505 yearly. This range reflects the compensation we reasonably expect to offer at the time of posting. Actual compensation will vary based on factors such as location, skills, experience, education, and internal equity. Because we operate across multiple U.S. markets, pay may differ depending on the cost of labor in specific locations. In addition to base salary, this position may be eligible for bonus, overtime or other forms of compensation and we offer a comprehensive benefits package that supports well-being, professional development, and work-life balance. Our recruiters are happy to share more about the specific salary range and total rewards package applicable to your location during the hiring process.

**Where People Flourish**

Our mission is to create sustainable societies where people and nature flourish. This means that a culture of inclusion is embedded in everything we do. Our people bring diverse backgrounds and experiences to the company, enabling us to deliver innovative and forward-thinking solutions to our clients. We also know how important it is to achieve the right balance of where, when, and how much you work. At Ramboll, we offer flexibility as part of our positive and inclusive approach to work. We are committed to equal employment opportunity, regardless of age, disability or medical condition, gender identity, marriage and domestic partnership, pregnancy and maternity, race, ancestry, or national origin, religion or belief, sex and sexual orientation, military service and veteran status, or any other protected characteristic. Ramboll wants to ensure opportunities are accessible to candidates with disabilities. So, please let us know if there are any changes we could make to the application process to make it more comfortable for you. You can contact us at job.advert.accessibility@ramboll.com with such requests.

**How to apply**

Apply online. Atta

### **Job Description and Duties**

Under the supervision of the Beaver Restoration Program Supervisor, the incumbent will serve as part of the Beaver Restoration Program, implementing beaver restoration projects to support ecosystem conservation, habitat restoration, species conservation, and improve climate change, drought, and wildfire resilience throughout California. jobs.title: Chemical Safety Specialist
jobs.description:
Under general supervision of the Chemical Hygiene Officer at the UCLA Office of Environment, Health & Safety and in accordance
  
with State & Federal regulations, the Chemical Safety Specialist applies technical knowledge to implement, administer, and
  
continuously improve comprehensive laboratory and chemical safety programs supporting research, (indirect) instructional, and
  
operational activities across UCLA. The incumbent provides technical consultation to the faculty, principal investigators,
  
researchers, staff, students, and campus departments regarding chemical, laboratory, and research safety requirements.

  

Responsibilities include developing and implementing Research Safety Management Plans; conducting lab hazard assessments
  
and compliance evaluations; developing and delivering safety training; participating in hazardous materials emergency response;
  
conducting incident investigations; supporting continuous process improvement initiatives; and performing other duties as
  
assigned.

  

Functional assignments may include support for research laboratories, engineering laboratories, medical and health sciences,
  
physical sciences, nanotechnology, hazardous materials, chemical hygiene, laboratory commissioning, laboratory design review,
  
or other specialized research safety programs.

  

This master job description establishes the core duties and responsibilities of the Laboratory Safety Professional position. Specific
  
program assignments, portfolios, departments, and specialized technical responsibilities may be assigned or modified by
  
management based on operational needs, organizational priorities, employee experience, and requirements. Such assignments
  
do not alter the overall classification or primary purpose of the position.

  

This is an in-person position.

  

The incumbent will work under general supervision and independently perform the full range of professional responsibilities
  
within assigned program areas. Their work is reviewed upon completion to ensure established standards are met and that
  
application of professional/technical judgment is sound, and for accuracy, consistency, and achievement of program objectives.

  
**Salary & Compensation**
  
  
\*UCLA provides a full pay range. Actual salary offers consider factors, including budget, prior experience, skills, knowledge, abilities, education, licensure and certifications, and other business considerations. Salary offers at the top of the range are not common. Visit UC Benefit package to discover benefits that start on day one, and UC Total Compensation Estimator to calculate the total compensation value with benefits.
  
**Qualifications**  
  

* 2 years professional experience in a comprehensive environmental health and safety program, or an equivalent combination of education and experience (Required)

* Ability to initiate and maintain cooperative working relationships with co-workers, supervisors, and managers. Skill in establishing rapport and gaining trust of others. Ability to work harmoniously and as a team player, thrive in a team-based environment, and skill in fostering teamwork among others. (Required)

* Skill in exchanging ideas, information, and opinions with others to formulate policies and programs and/or arrive jointly at decisions, conclusions, or solutions. Skill in working as part of a team; collaborating with colleagues. (Required)

* Ability to speak clearly on a one-to-one basis using appropriate vocabulary and grammar to obtain information, explain procedures and situations, and persuade others to comply with regulations and guidelines. Skill in speaking with persons of various social, cultural, economic and educational backgrounds. Description

Environmental Chemist

Put your analytical skills toward making a positive impact on the planet and your career! Join ICF in support of the US Environmental Protection Agency (USEPA) contract at the new Region 9 Laboratory in Corvallis, Oregon.

ICF is looking for an Environmental Laboratory Chemist in support of the USEPA Region 9 Environmental Services Assistance Team (ESAT) contract. ESAT provides analytical, quality assurance (QA), and technical support to USEPA programs such as Superfund and other programs requiring the identification, assessment, remediation, and regulation of environmental hazards. The team performs analysis on soil, water, air, waste, and tissue samples for chemical contaminants using USEPA-approved methods supporting EPA’s mission to protect human health and the environment through programs such as the Drinking Water programs, Clean Water Act (CWA), Clean Air Act (CAA), Superfund (CERCLA).

The Environmental Chemist
will apply their knowledge and work experience to primarily support the preparation and analysis of organic chemistry methods with possible cross-training on various inorganic analyses. All team activities must comply with EPA methods for various media (air, water, soil, biota) and environmental programs as well as the NELAC standard (2016). Job duties include sample preparation in support of and operation of GC-ECD, GC-FID, and GCMS to determine volatile and semivolatile organic compounds, pesticides, Aroclors, and fuel hydrocarbon as well as new and emerging contaminants. The successful candidate must be able to work both independently and as member of a team.

Required Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in chemistry, biology, environmental science, environmental engineering, or related.
4+ years of laboratory experience using EPA-approved methodologies and instrumentation, preferably GC-FID, GC-ECD and GC/MS.
Excellent verbal, interpersonal and written communication skills, and the ability to think critically.
U.S. citizenship required per federal contract.
MUST BE ABLE TO PASS an EPA background check to obtain access to US federal property.

Preferred Qualifications

Solvent extraction experience using EPA methodologies and CLLE, SPE, ASE and other techniques.
2-5 years of progressive experience in laboratories accredited for environmental analyses (e.g., TNI or NELAC, state programs).
Experience working at Federal facilities.
Laboratory Information Management Systems (LIMS) experience, knowledge of Promium Element LIMS is a plus.

The mission of the Chemical Analysis and Emissions Research Branch is to timely provide accurate measurements of mobile source emissions and fuels and technical expertise to support the California Air Resources Board motor vehicle and clean fuels programs.

The Fuel Analysis and Methods Evaluation Section (FAMES) is looking for an individual with strong work ethics, strong background in analytical chemistry, and good communication skills. The section analyzes motor vehicle fuels at the Southern California Head Quarters (SCHQ) in Riverside. The results are used in determining compliance with the cleaner burning gasoline and clean diesel regulations. FAMES also provides support to the Motor Vehicle Program by analyzing fuels used in emissions testing and providing expertise on the impact of fuel properties on emissions. Both functions require the evaluation, development, and implementation of more precise and accurate methods of analysis. FAMES is also responsible for proposing the adoption of new and updated methods into California regulations.

Under the supervision of an Air Resources Supervisor I, the successful candidate will carry out analyses of motor vehicle fuels using gas chromatography with flame ionization detector, supercritical fluid chromatograph, sulfur analyzer, x-ray fluorescence spectrometry, vapor pressure analyzer, and distillation analyzer. These analyses may be carried out at the SCHQ to prepare technical reports and scientific papers for presentation and publication and perform other duties as required. The candidate will also develop new test methods for the regulated fuel properties. Other duties include completing data and quality control reports, performing routine maintenance on the instruments, procuring supplies, managing service contracts, and developing new analytical methods or improving existing methods. An incumbent may also prepare and edit technical reports and scientific papers for publication and oversee the inventory and disposal of chemical reagents.

Job Summary

Langan is seeking an Air Quality Permitting and Dispersion Modeling Specialist
to join its collaborative team in any of our Langan locations. This individual will serve a key function in performing air quality projects for a wide range of clients throughout the US. Specific responsibilities will include preparation of emissions calculations, compliance reports, permit applications, and dispersion modeling using various programs (AERMOD, MOVES, etc.). In this role, you will have the opportunity to work with top industry leadership in a continuous learning environment.

Job Responsibilities

Provide technical support on air quality permitting projects, with special emphasis on air quality dispersion modeling development, execution, and analysis;
Have an understanding of and implement solutions to air quality impacts identified in air modeling analyses. This may include refining the model or working with clients to identify emission controls, operating modifications, or exhaust modifications;
Perform air quality modeling analyses using common air quality models (e.g., AERMOD, MOVES, CALPUFF, etc.) to evaluate air quality impacts as required for Title V, PSD, New Source Review compliance, and Environmental Impact Statements, as well as to support growing environmental concerns from the public associated with development projects;
Prepare and communicate technical work products clearly and effectively to clients and state and federal agencies at both a technical and business level; and,
Work as part of a multidisciplinary engineering team to support projects located throughout the US.

Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in Environmental or Chemical Engineering, Atmospheric Sciences/Meteorology or closely related field;
4+ years of experience working with air quality permitting and modeling;
Experience in performing air quality modeling using standard air quality models (e.g., AERMOD, CALPUFF, AERSCREEN, MOVES);
Demonstrated experience preparing permit applications and detailed emissions calculations;
PE or on track to obtain (FE/EIT) or other professional certification a plus;
Strong attention to detail with excellent analytical, judgment and problem-solving capabilities;
Demonstrated ability to work on a multidisciplinary team and succeed in a consulting environment;
Reliable transportation to access remote job sites and a valid driver’s license in good standing; and
Availability to work Monday through Friday with occasional evenings and weekends.

Description

DOES THIS DESCRIBE YOU?

You’re a technically strong, solutions-oriented air quality expert with a passion for advancing environmental outcomes in California. You’re confident working independently, especially when it comes to complex emissions modeling and health risk assessments using tools like CalEEMod, AERMOD, and HARP—but you’re also energized by collaboration and mentoring others. You possess a deep understanding of CEQA/NEPA air quality assessments and excel when helping clients navigate regulatory frameworks or crafting effective project strategies. You bring rigor to your work, care about getting the details right, and enjoy sharing your expertise to help elevate your team. If you're ready to bring leadership, vision, and technical excellence to impactful projects, we’d love to meet you.

Ascent is seeking a full-time Senior Air Quality Specialist, Technical Leader to join our AGENTs (Air Quality/Greenhouse Gas/Energy/Noise/Transportation) team in any of our offices: Berkeley, Irvine/Orange County, Lake Tahoe, Sacramento, or San Diego. In a typical week in this role, you might:

Independently conduct emissions modeling, including Health Risk Assessments using CalEEMod, Excel, AERMOD, EMFAC, HARP, and OFFROAD.
Conduct, review, and provide QA/QC feedback on emissions modeling from software, including but not limited to Calero, Excel, AERMOD, EMFAC, HARP, and OFFROAD.
Lead and direct marketing and business development pursuits, including developing capture strategies.
Lead the preparation of proposals for midsized projects and assist with proposals for larger projects, providing technical input, contributing to proposal writing through scope and cost development, identifying opportunities, and engaging with proposal/interview teams.
Collaborate with the AGENTs team to provide mentorship, build technical capabilities and services, ensure high-quality deliverables, and develop internal training materials and modeling protocols.
Work collaboratively with Ascent’s Environmental Practice Group to ensure timely delivery of technical work meeting Ascent’s quality standards.

Please note this job description is not designed to cover or contain a comprehensive listing of activities, duties, or responsibilities that are required of the employee for this job. Duties, responsibilities, and activities may change at any time with or without notice.

Requirements

Civil or environmental engineering, math, environmental science, atmospheric science, meteorology, geography, natural resources management, planning, or a related field.
A minimum of 8 years of direct professional experience conducting CEQA/NEPA air quality and GHG assessments.
Strong analytical, computer, spreadsheet, and writing skills are a must, and proficiency in emissions modeling software for development projects in California.
Successful candidates will have demonstrated experience running air quality emission models (EMFAC, CalEEMod, OFFROAD, MOVES) and dispersion models (CALINE-4, AERMOD, HARP) to evaluate project-related construction and operational emission and health impacts.
Candidate will have experience conducting emissions modeling QA/QC reviews, paying close attention to modeling methodologies and model accuracy.
Familiarity with state and federal air quality and climate change environmental policy and regulation, including CEQA, NEPA, and Clean Air Act, preferred.
Thorough understanding of the principles and practices, including meteorology, chemistry, and factors affecting air pollution distribution and effects.
Understanding of US EPA, California Air Resources Board, and local Air Quality Management District or Air Pollution Control District air quality regulatory programs and their relationship to the Federal and State Clean Air Acts.

Purpose Of The Position

We are currently seeking a Research Scientist to provide support to NASA SPoRT science and application activities related to leading machine learning activities in one or more of the following thematic areas: Air Quality/TEMPO, Wildland Fire, and Satellite Remote Sensing. The position will be located at the National Space Science & Technology Center in Huntsville, Alabama, and will support the scientific development and application of satellite remote sensing products.

SPoRT is a NASA project to transition unique observations and research capabilities to the operational weather community to improve short-term forecasts on a regional scale. Based at the NASA Marshall Space Flight Center in Huntsville, Alabama, SPoRT is collaborating with the University of Alabama in Huntsville to provide direct science support along with science and technical coordination in the areas of weather, climate, air quality, natural disasters, satellite remote sensing, and data science and applications.

Lead machine learning efforts in one or more of the following areas: air quality, wildland fire, and satellite remote sensing.
Provide scientific expertise to facilitate applied science studies in satellite remote sensing, health & air quality, or wildland fire.

Develop synergistic products from TEMPO, ABI, and GLM data to enhance science applications, with special attention to wildfire smoke and lightning NOx.
Lead the development of new proposals and scientific papers on machine learning, satellite remote sensing, and numerical modeling.

Understanding of remote sensing theory, satellite data applications, air pollution chemistry, and meteorological principles

jobs.title: Executive Associate Dean, College of Agriculture, Food and Environmental Sciences
jobs.description:
Job Summary

The Executive Associate Dean is a senior academic leader and strategic advisor to the dean and a key member of the college's executive leadership team. Bringing the perspective and judgment of an accomplished faculty member and academic administrator, the Executive Associate Dean maintains a broad, integrated view of the college's academic programs, people, operations, partnerships, resources and priorities; identifies connections, opportunities and emerging issues across those areas; and provides strategic counsel to the dean on matters affecting the college and its long-term success.

Working closely with the dean, associate and assistant deans, department heads, center directors and other college leaders, the Executive Associate Dean helps translate college priorities into coordinated action and ensures that executive decision-making is informed by academic context, institutional knowledge and the perspectives of faculty and academic leaders. The position serves as a trusted advisor and sounding board to the dean, provides leadership on complex issues that span organizational and disciplinary boundaries, and represents and acts on behalf of the dean as appropriate.

In addition to this collegewide leadership role, the Executive Associate Dean provides executive oversight of academic operations, agricultural and commercial operations, facilities and land-use planning, and other designated areas of college operations.

Department Summary

The College of Agriculture, Food and Environmental Sciences (CAFES) at Cal Poly is one of the nation’s premier colleges of agriculture and natural resources – and the fifth-largest of its kind in the U.S. With more than 4,200 undergraduates, 16 majors, five graduate programs, and 192 dedicated faculty and staff, CAFES is a powerhouse of innovation, impact and hands-on learning. Our signature Learn by Doing philosophy comes alive across 10,000 acres of cropland, pastures, orchards, vineyards, and forests, as well as in specialized teaching and research facilities. From the Animal Health Center and Equine Center to the Center for Wine and Viticulture, Ag Tech Center and Plant Sciences Complex at the San Luis Obispo campus and Marine Transportation facilities at the Solano campus, students and faculty work side by side – tackling real-world challenges and shaping the future of food, agriculture and the environment. Discover more at cafes.calpoly.edu .

Key Qualifications

Exceptional written and verbal communication skills and the ability to work effectively with academic, administrative, industry and community audiences.
Demonstrated ability to think strategically and institutionally across academic disciplines, programs and administrative functions.
Excellent leadership and management skills, including the ability to build alignment, develop others and lead through influence as well as formal authority.
A leadership style characterized by integrity, openness, flexibility, inclusiveness, transparency and kindness.
Demonstrated ability to synthesize complex and sometimes competing information and perspectives and translate them into sound recommendations for executive decision-making.
Demonstrated capacity to serve as a trusted advisor to senior leadership, including the judgment and confidence to offer candid counsel, constructive challenge and alternative perspectives.
Ability to move effectively between strategic and operational perspectives and recognize when an operational issue has broader academic, organizational, financial or reputational implications.
Record of successfully addressing complex issues that cross organizational, disciplinary or functional boundaries.
Demonstrated use of tact and diplomacy to effectively handle a broad range of high level and sensitive interpersonal situations with diverse personalities and to respond appropriately to conflicts and problems.
Ability to work well under pressure and maintain composure.

Education And Experience

PhD or terminal degree
Credentials appropriate for a tenured appointment at the rank of full professor within the College of Agriculture, Food and Environmental Sciences
At least five years of relevant higher education administrative experience with evidence of increasing responsibility. Examples include service as an associate dean, department head or chair, program director or coordinator, center director, or leader of a sufficiently complex research or academic program.
Distinguished record of academic achievement and demonstrated effectiveness in teaching, research and service
Record of successful leadership of people, programs and complex initiatives
Demonstrated experience working across academic disciplines, programs or organizational units to advance shared priorities
Demonstrated understanding of faculty roles, academic culture, shared governance and the opportunities and challenges of leadership in a complex university environment
Commitment to collegial, collaborative and constructive interactions across the college and university

Licenses, Certificates, Credentials

Possession of a valid driver’s license or the ability to obtain by date of hire

The anticipated hiring range for this role is $210,000 - $230,000. Note that the offer is calculated based on the background and relevant years of experience of the individual selected.

Factors in determining the appropriate compensation for a role include experience, skills, knowledge, abilities, education, licensure and certifications, and other business and organizational needs. The Classification Range may be broader than what the University anticipates paying for this position, based on internal equity, budget, and collective bargaining agreements (when applicable).

Known for its Learn by Doing philosophy, Cal Poly is ranked among the top 10 public universities in the nation. Each year, more than 23,000 top-tier students come to Cal Poly in San Luis Obispo and Cal Poly Maritime Academy in Solano County to put knowledge into action, taking their learning outside the classroom as they prepare for careers in engineering, agriculture, science, business, humanities, maritime and the built environment. Overview:

**ROLE AT A GLANCE:**  
The Principal Scientist, Toxicology will provide technical support in substantiating the safety of ingredients, formulas and packaging used in Herbalife inner and outer nutrition products in all stages of product lifecycle to support sustainable business growth. The Principal Scientist, Toxicology will work independently to conduct safety evaluation of ingredients, formulations and packaging, prepare appropriate documentation that meets standards and requirements for product safety and regulatory acceptability. This position will work closely with a wide range of regional and corporate teams across organization to ensure safety compliance of Herbalife products worldwide.

In addition, this position is expected to participate in external trade and science-based initiatives pertaining to the safety of product categories relevant to Herbalife business and leverage external partners to advance the science and brand of Herbalife products. The Principal Scientist is a key position in R&D and must inspire and energize employees through advanced knowledge of toxicology, personal leadership, influence, and thorough planning and drive for timely and appropriate results. This position may need to travel globally up to 10% of time.

**HOW YOU’LL MAKE AN IMPACT:**  

* Critically review, validate and summarize scientific evidence for assessing safety of proposed product formulas and materials (including food and dietary ingredients, additives, personal care ingredients, and their constituents) and provide recommendations to address evidence gaps (if any) to support product development and innovation with minimum supervision.
* Develop safety substantiation for Herbalife’s ingredients and finished products, and prepare written technical reports (e.g. risk assessments, safety monographs, etc.) that meet Herbalife internal standards and regulatory acceptability.
* Use published toxicological frameworks and regulatory guidance documents to perform and review hazard, safety and risk assessments to meet applicable regulatory requirements.
* Prepare responses to inquiries regarding the safety of Herbalife’s ingredients and products from regulatory bodies and customers in the local countries where Herbalife products are marketed.
* Lead and provide support in the design, conduct and evaluation of toxicology studies on existing and new ingredients and formulations with training.
* Lead stakeholder in preparation of requisite toxicological requirements for GRAS dossier preparation for North America and Novel Foods applications for Europe.
* Guide and review the development of safety-based specifications for raw materials and finished products, and advisory label statement review process.
* Communicate product and ingredient safety information verbally and in writing to internal customers, including Formulation, Scientific Affairs, Government Affairs, Regulatory Affairs, Quality Assurance, and Post-market Safety Surveillance departments.
* Perform risk assessment and modeling of chemicals using established toxicological databases and tools such as OHAT systematic review, Benchmark Dose Software, Tox21, AOP and QSAR Toolbox under guidance.
* Remain abreast of current risk assessment methodologies and toxicological sciences relevant to Herbalife product categories and communicate emerging topics and potential implications to internal stakeholders.
* Represent Herbalife’s key business interests on trade association task forces, identify and pursue external Key Opinion Leaders for research collaboration opportunities, and support strategic external engagement with scientific and regulatory communities.
* Communicate critical issues to direct manager and other relevant parties in a timely manner, with recommended solutions including timelines and required resources.
* Follows Company policies, processes and procedures, and performs all duties in an honest, ethical and professional manner.
* Additional duties as assigned.

**LEADERSHIP AND SUPERVISORY RESPONSIBILITIES:**  

* N/A

Qualifications:

**QUALIFICATIONS FOR SUCCESS:**

**Education**  

* Master or Doctorate Degree in Toxicology, Pharmacology, or related discipline

**Experience**

The network can provide full-service Environment Testing capabilities in all US states, either via direct local laboratory participation, or via the extensive logistics network. Through our sustained investment in people, technology, instrumentation, and infrastructure, Eurofins Environment Testing laboratories are positioned to support public and private sectors, DoD, DOE and Municipalities. Job Description

The Courier is responsible for the pick-up and delivery of water, soil and air samples to and from the laboratory. Maintain the quality, hold time, and turnaround time objectives of the lab. Prepare and deliver bottle orders to clients following the SOP of the lab. Receive and stock all sample control supplies, prepare and ship sample kits and perform sampling events as needed. Dispose of samples and hazardous waste according to guidelines and carry out any other duties assigned by the department manager.

The Courier will work out of the Concord, New Hampshire lab. We are looking for (2) Full time Couriers. Mon-Fri 7:00am- 3:30pm and 11:00am to 7:30pm.

Do you enjoy Driving? Like Seeing Different Parts of NH, VT, MA and ME? Employee will drive 200-300 miles during their shift.

Compensation $16/hour plus benefits

Courier responsibilities include, but are not limited to, the following

Perform all duties as outlined in the SOP for Couriers.
Pick up and deliver samples, bottle orders and report to the laboratory for sign-in and analysis.
Count the number of samples when receiving them from clients to make sure that the Chain of Custody and samples match. Verify that samples are not broken or damaged.
Receive and sign the Chain of Custody.
Ensure that client signs, dates, and records time on the Chain of Custody when releasing samples.
Transport samples on ice from client site to the lab, or from our lab to a sub- contracted laboratory.
Unload samples and inspect for damage or violated hold times to maintain sample integrity.
Interact with Project Managers and clients appropriately and professionally.
Follow directions or use maps to locate client offices/sites as specified in the courier request form.
Communicate effectively with the courier coordinator about the courier schedule.

Restock supplies when received so supplies are available to employees when needed.

Comply with the Company’s “Driver Evaluation and Qualification Policy”.
Maintain the shipping/receiving area to ensure a safe work environment.
Prepare outgoing shipments of bottle kits and coolers for pick-up.
Perform on-site sampling events as needed.
Dispose of samples according to guidelines on a monthly basis to remain in compliance with EPA and EH&S requirements.
Maintain delivery truck to keep in proper working order.
Label samples after log in on an as needed basis.

High school diploma or equivalent
Authorization to work in the United States indefinitely without restriction or sponsorship
A valid state issued driver’s license is required as an employee with driving responsibilities. Clean driving record to drive company vehicle.
Ability to lift up to 50 pounds. Samples will be in coolers packed in ice.
Professional working proficiency in English is a requirement, including the ability to read, write and speak in English.
Basic computer skills.

Ability to read maps and follow directions
Ability to operate a motor vehicle
Ability to prioritize
Excellent communication (oral and written) and attention to detail
Ability to work independently and as part of a team, self-motivation, adaptability, and a positive attitude
Ability to learn new techniques, perform multiple tasks simultaneously, keep accurate records, follow instructions, and comply with company policies

jobs.title: Environmental Health Program Supervisor
jobs.description:
The Environmental Health Services Division of San Mateo County Health is seeking well-qualified candidates for the position of Environmental Health Program Supervisor.
Program Supervisors, under direction, supervise, direct, organize, manage, evaluate, audit, and provide accountability for one or more Environmental Health programs in the consumer protection (food, water, housing, vector control, land use, pools, solid waste, infectious waste, and cross connections) or hazardous materials/hazardous waste areas.

Currently, there are two regular vacancies in the Environmental Health Services Division's Consumer Protection Food/Pool Programs and Waste Programs. These positions are located in San Mateo, but will travel/drive throughout the county to perform the duties of the job.

The position in the Consumer Protection Food/Pool Program supervises staff that inspect food sold in markets, restaurants, schools, mobile catering facilities, and special events; educate the public and businesses about proper sanitation and food handling; follow-up on complaints and reports of food-borne illness; provide information on food establishment compliance; inspect public recreational water areas such as swimming pools/spas for health and safety compliance; and verify that businesses selling tobacco products have the appropriate permits.

The position in the Waste Programs supervises staff that inspect solid waste operations such as landfills, transfer stations, Post-Closure Landfill Development projects, medical waste generators, body art facilities and practitioners, and massage establishments. This position also supervises household hazardous waste collection operations for residents and small businesses and implements the County ‘s Safe Medicine Disposal Ordinance.

The ideal candidate
is:

Enthusiastic for and dedicated to public service.
Experienced in working for a regulatory agency with a working knowledge of California Retail Food Code (California Health and Safety Code Division 104, Part 7), FDA Standards, California Swimming Pool Code (California Code of Regulations, Title 22 Division 4).
Experienced in working for a Local Enforcement Agency with working knowledge of solid waste regulatory requirements (California Code of Regulations, Title 14 and 27), the Safe Body Art Act (California Health and Safety Code Division 104, Part 15, Chapter 17), the Medical Waste Management Act (California Health and Safety Code, Division 104, Part 14), and County Code for massage establishments, safe medicine disposal and body art. Experienced in directing hazardous waste operations, ensuring compliance with State requirements and incorporating safety practices.
At least three years of experience related to performing inspections, investigations, and research for an environmental health program in a regulatory agency.
Experience in leading and motivating a team.
Approachable and politically astute with a supervisory style that quickly fosters trust, loyalty, respect and commitment from employees.
An experienced REHS with a thorough understanding of the full range of issues, practices and regulations related to consumer protection.
An innovative leader who has collaborated with other agencies with positive outcomes that benefited public health and public education.
Technologically savvy and knowledgeable of electronic field inspection systems and other computer-based technologies utilized by regulatory agencies.
Highly focused and organized, capable of establishing and implementing program budgets.
An excellent problem-solver with superior oral and written communication skills.
A productive team member, willing and able to coordinate closely with other program supervisors to ensure a standard and efficient implementation of programs.

Examples Of Duties

Duties may include, but are not limited to, the following:

Manage, audit, and standardize activities in assigned program area.
Within a team concept, organize and supervise the activities of professional staff.
Participate in the hiring of assigned staff, recommending selection for management approval.
Evaluate employee performance, counsel employees, and effectively recommend initial disciplinary actions and other personnel decisions.
Assist in training and orientation of new personnel.
Evaluate program needs and recommend budget changes and allocations.
Keep current on developments in field of expertise through participation in professional organizations, attending training programs, and reviewing current legislation.
Develop/maintain program guides for assigned program area.
Maintain liaison with federal, state and local officials regarding standards and regulations; serve as advisor to agencies, commissions and other groups on environmental health issues and problems.
Make presentations to city, county, and special district councils/boards, citizen groups, business owners and others on environmental health issues and programs.
Interpret and enforce state and local laws, ordinances, regulations, and codes in areas of environmental health pertaining to assigned program area.
Evaluate workload of personnel and effectiveness of program in assigned area and prepare reports with recommendations for program modifications.
Review proposed legislation; prepare and review administrative and technical reports and studies reports and studies.
Confer with management on significant program issues, needs, conflicts, problems and accomplishments.
Perform other duties as assigned.

Qualifications

Knowledge of:

The environmental health provisions of the California Health and Safety Code, and the rules and regulations of the State Department of Health Services pertaining to environmental health standards and local ordinances.
Public health/environmental health inspection and investigation principles, practices, and administrative procedures.
The principles and techniques of program management.

Skill/Ability to:

Plan, organize and supervise the work of others.
Manage programs in a team environment.
Train others in the principles and techniques of enforcement work.
Define difficult problem areas, analyze complex data and make valid recommendations.
Establish and maintain cooperative working relationships with others.
Speak effectively and make public presentations.
Prepare clear, concise reports and correspondence.

Experience and Education:

Any combination of education and experience that would likely provide the required knowledge, skills and abilities is qualifying. A typical way to qualify is:

Four years increasingly responsible experience as an Environmental Health Specialist or Hazardous Materials Specialist, which includes two years experience in a regulatory agency.

Licensure/Certification:

Possession of a California certificate as a Registered Environmental Health Specialist within two years from date of hire.
Possession and maintenance of a valid Class C California driver license or equivalent.

Job Description And Duties

The mission of the Chemical Analysis and Emissions Research Branch is to timely provide accurate measurements of mobile source emissions and fuels and technical expertise to support the California Air Resources Board (CARB) motor vehicle and clean fuels programs.

The Fuel Analysis and Methods Evaluation Section (FAMES) is looking for an individual with strong work ethics, strong background in analytical chemistry, and good communication skills. The section analyzes motor vehicle fuels at the Southern California Head Quarters in Riverside. The results are used in determining compliance with the cleaner burning gasoline and clean diesel regulations. FAMES also provides support to the Motor Vehicle Program by analyzing fuels used in emissions testing and providing expertise on the impact of fuel properties on emissions. Both functions require the evaluation, development, and implementation of more precise and accurate methods of analysis. FAMES is also responsible for proposing the adoption of new and updated methods into California regulations.

Under the direction of the FAMES Manager, the Staff Air Pollution Specialist serves as an independent technical expert to oversee fuels analyses and methods. In addition, the incumbent will apply engineering principles to perform the more complex work of evaluating fuel effects on vehicle emissions and develop test methods for the fuel regulations when the need arises. Duties include evaluating and improving fuel analysis test methods; conducting fuel sample analysis; and overseeing the fuel analysis work conducted by other staff, conducting second-level quality control on reported data, reviewing literature studies related to fuel effect issues, and developing test plans to investigate fuel impacts. The incumbent will be responsible for data analysis, interpretation, reports, and oral presentations to stakeholders. jobs.description:
**Position Information**
------------------------

**Sonoma Water is seeing a passionate and driven Environmental Specialist I professional to join our team!**  
**Join us in protecting and enhancing Sonoma County’s natural resources through meaningful, impactful work.**

  

The Sonoma Water Agency is seeking a qualified candidate to fill a Water Agency Environmental Specialist I position responsible for working on environmental compliance and permitting matters for Sonoma Water projects.

At Sonoma Water, Environmental Specialists are responsible for evaluating, analyzing, and reporting on the environmental impacts of water supply, flood control, sanitation, and sustainability projects. To comply with federal, state, and local regulations, these positions assist in developing and proposing mitigation strategies to avoid, reduce, or offset the environmental impacts of projects. The Environmental Specialist I also uses an interdisciplinary approach from applied knowledge of biology, ecology, environmental science, and hydrology to:  
  
  

* Assist with the preparation of California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) studies, such as categorical exemptions, mitigated negative declarations, environmental impact reports, and technical resource reports
* Assist with preparation of environmental regulatory permit applications to local, state, and federal resource agencies
* Perform field assessments and surveys for sensitive resources, such as aquatic and terrestrial habitat features, wildlife, botanical, and fisheries resources to evaluate environmental effects and determine potential impacts from projects
* Review natural resource studies and reports to understand historical and current site conditions of a project
* Review project information, schedules, studies, and designs, and assist in preparing tracking tools, standard operating procedures, and reports for projects
* Assist in the preparation and review of documents to comply with state, federal, and local environmental laws and regulations; land use planning projects; grant applications; and right-of-way activities
* Stay up to date with environmental laws such as the CEQA, National Environmental Protection Act (NEPA), Clean Water Act, Porter-Cologne Water Quality Control Act, California and Federal Endangered Species Acts

  
The ideal candidate for this position is a team player and passionate about the environment and its resources. They will possess strong communication, problem-solving, and project organizational skills. In addition, they will possess experience conducting many of the following activities:

* Knowledge of and experience with handling threatened, endangered, and/or sensitive species listed under state or federal endangered species acts (such as California red-legged frog, California tiger salamander, steelhead trout, and California freshwater shrimp)
* Conducting field assessments and investigations for natural resources such as aquatic and terrestrial habitat features, wildlife and botanical resources in remote areas (e.g. agricultural lands, meadowlands, forests, and aquatic and riparian habitats)
* Collecting, analyzing, and reporting on environmental scientific data associated with natural resources, specifically wildlife
* Researching the historical land uses, existing conditions, and natural resources of a project site, and associated local, state, and federal regulations applicable to the resources and project
* Preparation of CEQA and/or NEPA compliance documents for public projects
* Applying for and acquiring environmental regulatory permits from local, state, and federal resource agencies
* Reviewing the development of public projects (specifically water utility projects) and their associated schedules, studies, and designs
* Collaborating with planners, engineers, contractors, and consultants on the design and construction of public projects (specifically water utility projects)

**Note: This position typically works Monday-Friday during regular business hours but may be required to work evening, weekend, or holiday shifts to conduct field investigations, help with biological seasonal monitoring, and attend public meetings or community events.**

  
  

**About Sonoma Water**
  
Sonoma Water is a special district formed by the California State Legislature in 1949 and is responsible for providing a safe and reliable water supply to its customers in Sonoma and Marin counties. Sonoma Water also maintains 75 miles of flood control channels and provides sanitation services. Employing approximately 250 employees, Sonoma Water consists of four divisions, including Engineering & Resource Planning, Environmental Resources, Business Services & External Affairs, and Water/Wastewater Operations & Maintenance. Sonoma Water supports the concept of environmental sustainability, focusing on renewable power sources, and strives to be a leader in its water use efficiency and fishery restoration programs.
  
  
Employees of Sonoma Water are employees of a special district and are not subject to the provisions of the Civil Service Ordinance of the County of Sonoma.**What We Offer**

Working at the County of Sonoma offers expansive opportunities for growth and development, the ability to be a part of a challenging and rewarding work environment, and the satisfaction of knowing you're working to better our communities. You can also look forward to flexible work arrangements and excellent benefits\* including:

* **Hybrid Telework** - A schedule that meets the needs of our staff, department operations, and the communities we serve may be available depending on the assignment
* **Salary Advancement** - A salary increase after 1,040 hours (6 months when working full-time) for good work performance; eligibility for a salary increase for good performance every year thereafter, until reaching the top of the salary range
* **Paid Time Off** - Competitive vacation and sick leave accruals, 12 paid holidays, and an additional 8 floa

**Company Description**  

Ramboll is a global architecture, engineering, and consultancy company. As a foundation\-owned people company, founded in Denmark, we believe that the purpose of sustainable change is to create a thriving world for both nature and people. So, that’s where we start – and how we work. Our history is rooted in a clear vision of how a responsible company should act and being open and curious is a cornerstone of our culture. Ramboll in the Americas has thousands of experts working across more than 70 offices. Ramboll experts deliver innovative solutions across Environment \& Health, Water, Energy, and Planning \& Urban Design.

 **Job Description**  

Applicants must be currently authorized to work in the United States on a full\-time basis. No sponsorship is available for this position.


Are you eager to develop your technical and professional excellence and advance your career in a collaborative, inclusive, diverse, and empowering culture? Ramboll is a leading scientific and environmental consulting firm providing a broad range of technical services to both public and private sector clients. When you join Ramboll, you will become part of a company that strives to make a difference – for our employees, clients, and society.


Ramboll is seeking an entry\-level to mid\-level consultant to join the Risk Assessment and Community Health group in one of the firm’s Oakland, CA office. Hybrid work arrangements are available, with office presence required at least two days a week.

**Your new role**


As an entry\-level health sciences consultant at Ramboll, you will support a range of human health risk assessment and community health projects in a collaborative, fast\-paced environment. Your work will include independent, detail\-oriented technical tasks as well as coordination with colleagues and project teams. Projects may be related to hazardous waste and other contaminated sites, Brownfield redevelopment, vapor intrusion, ambient and indoor air quality, product safety, regulatory interactions, community engagement, and litigation. Tasks may include data management, statistical analysis, fate and transport modeling, spatial analysis, sampling/remediation/risk management planning, and technical reporting. This is a unique opportunity to work with Ramboll experts to advance your technical and consulting skills.

**Your key responsibilities will be:**

* Compiling, organizing, and managing environmental data and databases; performing statistical and geospatial analyses of environmental and health data.
* Evaluating the environmental fate and transport of chemicals
* Estimating human exposures to chemicals in different environmental media (e.g., air, soil, sediment, fish tissue, produce, water, etc.) and exposure scenarios, and calculating associated health risks.
* Assisting with preparation of technical reports, written communication, proposals, and presentations
* Reviewing and evaluating technical documents (e.g., scientific articles, regulations)

  

**Qualifications** **About you**


From the moment you start at Ramboll, we will support your professional development and advancement in the company! Successful candidates will typically possess:

* Advanced degree (M.S., MPH or equivalent) in Environmental Science or Engineering, Environmental Health Science and/or Environmental Toxicology
* Exemplary individuals with bachelor’s degree and 2 \+ years of relevant experience may be considered.
* Strong analytical, quantitative, organizational, problem\-solving, critical thinking skills, and time management skills; excellent written and oral communication skills
* 2\+ years of chemistry coursework required.
* Current authorization to work in the United States on a full\-time basis, where required for the position.


Preferred Skills and Experience:

* Knowledge of risk assessment, exposure assessment, and fate and transport of chemicals in the environment
* Proficiency with MS Office; experience with MS Access or other relational databases (e.g., SQL) for managing, querying, and analyzing environmental data.
* Demonstrated strong quantitative and problem\-solving skills; experienced with statistical and data analysis using R, Python, SQL, or SAS
* GIS capability is a plus.
* Experience reviewing and evaluating technical documents, scientific articles, regulations, and regulatory guidance.

  

**Additional Information** **What we can offer you**

* Meaningful, high\-impact work
* Flexible and hybrid work arrangements
* Competitive compensation and benefits
* Professional development and leadership opportunities
* A collaborative and inclusive culture
* The long\-term thinking of a foundation\-owned company

**Salary Transparency Statement**


At Ramboll, we are committed to fair and transparent compensation practices that support our people and our purpose of creating sustainable societies. The anticipated base salary range for this position is $79,040–$98,800 per year. This range reflects the compensation we reasonably expect to offer at the time of posting. Actual compensation will vary based on factors such as location, skills, experience, education, and internal equity. Because we operate across multiple U.S. markets, pay may differ depending on the cost of labor in specific locations. In addition to base salary, this position may be eligible for bonus, overtime or other forms of compensation and we offer a comprehensive benefits package that supports well\-being, professional development, and work\-life balance. jobs.description:
##### **About Peraton**


Peraton is a next\-generation national security company that drives missions of consequence spanning the globe and extending to the farthest reaches of the galaxy. As the world’s leading mission capability integrator and transformative enterprise IT provider, we deliver trusted, highly differentiated solutions and technologies to protect our nation and allies. Peraton operates at the critical nexus between traditional and nontraditional threats across all domains: land, sea, space, air, and cyberspace. The company serves as a valued partner to essential government agencies and supports every branch of the U.S. armed forces. Each day, our employees solve the most daunting challenges that our customers face. Visit peraton.com to learn how we’re keeping people around the world safe and secure.


##### **Program Overview**


Provide critical communications and tracking for multiple spacecraft from three complexes located globally, and operates year round 24 hours/7days to provide continuous contact with the spacecraft. The program fulfills NASA goals by supporting NASA deep space mission set, including NASA\-funded missions and collaborative international missions.
##### **About The Role**


Peraton is seeking an **Environmental Analyst** to support our Deep Space Network (DSN) Operations and Maintenance contract with NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory in Fort Irwin, CA.

  

The Deep Space Network is NASA’s international array of giant radio antennas that supports interplanetary spacecraft missions, plus a few that orbit Earth. The DSN also provides radar and radio astronomy observations that improve our understanding of the solar system and the larger universe. The antennas of the Deep Space Network are the indispensable link to explorers venturing beyond the moon. They provide the crucial connection for commanding our spacecraft and receiving their never\-before\-seen images and scientific information on Earth, propelling our understanding of the universe, our solar system and ultimately, our place within it.

  

**Responsibilities:**

  

The Environmental Analyst supports and manages environmental compliance programs, regulatory reporting, data analysis, inspections, and permitting. The role requires the ability to interpret federal, state, and local environmental regulations and translate them into practical compliance programs, working closely with EHS, operations, engineering, facilities, maintenance, and management.

  

**Compliance and Reporting:**


* Monitor compliance with federal, state, and local environmental regulations, including those administered by the EPA, state agencies, air quality management districts, and water quality boards
* Conduct compliance inspections and assessments, identify gaps, and develop corrective actions
* Maintain environmental permits, licenses, registrations, records, and regulatory documentation
* Prepare and submit required environmental reports and notifications
* Track regulatory changes and evaluate their impact on operations
* Support environmental audits and agency inspections
  

**Air Quality and Wastewater:**


* Support air permitting and compliance, including records for emissions, permitted equipment, and operating parameters
* Assist with emissions calculations, testing, monitoring, and corrective actions
* Support industrial and sanitary wastewater compliance programs
  

**Environmental Management and Incident Response:**


* Support development and maintenance of environmental management systems and continuous improvement initiatives
* Investigate and document environmental incidents, spills, and releases; coordinate corrective and preventive actions
* Support regulatory notifications, agency communications, and emergency response involving environmental releases
##### **Qualifications**


**Required Qualifications:**

  

* BS/BA and 2 years of experience; or MS/MA and 0 years; or 6 years with no degree
* Strong working knowledge of EPA regulations and applicable federal, state, and local environmental requirements
* Experience conducting environmental inspections, audits, and compliance assessments
* Experience with environmental reporting and regulatory documentation
* Strong analytical, organizational, and communication skills, with the ability to manage multiple regulatory deadlines independently
* Proficiency with Microsoft Excel and Word
* U.S. citizenship with proof of citizenship; must be able to obtain a trusted background check and pass a National Criminal Information Check (NCIC)
* Must possess and retain a valid California Real ID driver's license
  

**Preferred Qualifications:**

  

* Bachelor's degree in Environmental Science, Environmental Engineering, Chemistry, Biology, Occupational Safety, or a related field
* Experience with California Environmental Regulations and agencies such as Cal/OSHA, DTSC, Mojave Desert or South Coast AQMD, and Regional Water Quality Control Boards
* Experience with hazardous waste, air quality, stormwater, wastewater, SPCC, and environmental permitting
* Experience with environmental management systems (ISO 14001\) and EHS data management software
* Experience developing compliance procedures and training programs
* Professional certification such as CHMM or CEP
  
##### **Details**


**Target Salary Range:** $51,000 \- $82,000\. This represents the typical salary range for this position. Salary is determined by various factors, including but not limited to, the scope and responsibilities of the position, the individual’s experience, education, knowledge, skills, and competencies, as well as geographic location and business and contract considerations. Depending on the position, employees may be eligible for overtime, shift differential, and a discretionary bonus in addition to base pay.

Are you interested in contributing to the protection of California's natural resources? Come join CDFW and help us expand our statewide ecological data network! Under close supervision of project managers Wildlife Branch Lands Program, the incumbent performs a variety of duties leading the installation, management, and data analysis of climate and biodiversity sensors for the CDFW Climate\-Biodiversity Sentinel Site network throughout California. The program aims to assess the potential impacts of climate change on biodiversity in support of the Department’s mission. Duties include planning and leading routine field visits focused on the installation and maintenance of climate sensors, camera traps, acoustic recorders, and Motus towers that are used to track migratory wildlife. jobs.description:
PLZ is committed to product stewardship and innovation, strong ethical standards, sustainable operations and most importantly, the development of our people. Whether at our manufacturing facilities or corporate headquarters, PLZ prioritizes health and safety, and offers you the support you need to create the career you want, through engagement, equity and inclusion, and opportunity.



From household cleaning solutions to personal care products, and food to automotive lubricants, PLZ produces more than 2,500 different aerosol and liquid products in our facilities across the continent. We know that being the partner of choice for our clients starts with being the partner of choice for our employees. Learn more at www.plzcorp.com/careers (http://www.plzcorp.com/careers) or visit https://youtu.be/XYNIFpLQIJY (https://youtu.be/XYNIFpLQIJY)


The **Environmental Specialist** will ensure environmental compliance matters, including periodic inspections, sampling, and reporting, are completed according to schedule. Support the EHS Manager on environmental health \& safety matters. Identify training needs and deliver to department employees. Conduct and maintain reporting as needed for the PLZ Team.


***Key Responsibility:***


* Ensure compliance with Federal, State, Local environmental laws, regulations and PLZ procedures.
* Manage Clean Air Act (CAA) Title V, new source review, and/or minor source permit compliance, including emissions reporting and compliance documentation.
* Assist site EHS Managers with the Clean Water Act (CWA) National Pollutant Discharge Elimination System (NPDES) water permits (Industrial and Stormwater), compliance, training, and reporting.
* Assist site EHS Managers with Spill Prevention, Control and Countermeasure (SPCC) plan management and training.
* Assist site EHS Manager with Resource Recovery and Conservation Act (RCRA) and chemical container management program. Develop RCRA training, guidance documents and procedures as necessary.
* Assist site EHS Managers with Emergency Planning and Community Right\-to\-Know (EPCRA) data collection and filing EPCRA 311/312 (Tier II) and EPCRA 313 (Toxic Release Inventory) reports. Develop EPCRA training, guidance documents and procedures as necessary.
* Assist site EHS Manager with air permit recordkeeping and reporting.
* Assist site EHS Manager with maintaining a chemical inventory.
* Act as resource for RMP program compliance.
* Encourage and promote good environmental practices.
* Support continuous improvement on all aspects of environmental health \& safety.


***Knowledge, skills, and abilities:***

* Strong verbal and written communication skills, receive, and provide clear instructions.
* Must possess the ability to make independent contributions, provide leadership and drive change.
* Must be computer literate and proficient in the use of Microsoft Office programs and other software such as: WORD, EXCEL, POWERPOINT, TEAMS, ADOBE products
* SAP proficiency is strongly desired.


***Qualifications:***

* Bachelor’s degree with focus in environmental engineering (preferred), environmental science or environmental, health and safety.
* Minimum of 3 years related experience in an environmental compliance capacity in an industrial environment preferably within process manufacturing, petrochemical or chemical manufacturing.


***Supervisory Responsibilities:***


* This position is responsible for managing the chemical handler assigned to the chemical storage and disposal area.


***Work Environment:***


* Fast\-paced manufacturing environment.
* Work in a production area with fast\-moving equipment, moderate to high noise levels, and temperature changes.
* Perform occasional lifting, bending, grasping, reaching, pulling, climbing, and computer use as needed.


***Compensation:***

Our compensation reflects the cost of labor across several US geographic markets. The base pay for this position ranges from $72,000/year in our lowest geographic market up to $90,000/year in our highest geographic market. Pay is based on a number of factors including market location and may vary depending on job\-related knowledge, skills, and experience. Dependent on the position offered, other forms of compensation may be provided as part of a total compensation package, in addition to a full range of medical, financial, and/or other benefits.


***PLZ Corp offers a robust suite of benefits including:***


* Medical, Dental \& Vision benefits.
* Company paid Life and Short\-Term disability.
* Voluntary benefits including additional life, disability, and hospital/accident insurance.
* 401k \& company provided match.
* Paid Time Off
* Bonus incentive programs (Note, bonuses are subject to the rules governing the program, whereby an award, if any, depends on various factors, including, without limitation, individual and organizational performance.)


*All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, gender identity, disability, protected veteran status or other protected status. EEOE/M/F/Vet/Disabled. All your information will be kept confidential according to EEO guidelines.*


Equal Opportunity Employer

jobs.description:
**About the role:**


The Environmental Public Health and Water team supports Victoria's Chief Health Officer Group in providing specialist expertise on the public health impacts of environmental hazards.



The work is interesting and diverse and can involve dealing with unusual and unexpected or emerging environmental hazards and scenarios. The team provides advice on risk management, policy options and complex environmental public health issues, working under the *Public Health and Wellbeing Act 2008*, *Public Health and Wellbeing Regulations 2019*, *Safe Drinking Water Act 2003*, *Safe Drinking Water Regulations 2025* and *Health (Fluoridation) Act 1973*.


**About us:**


At the Victorian Department of Health we want a future where Victorians are the healthiest people in the world. A Victoria where our children and people thrive, our workplaces are productive and safe, and our communities are more connected.


We see it as our job to support Victorians to stay healthy and safe. And to deliver a world\-class healthcare system that ensures every single Victorian can access safe, quality care that leads to better health outcomes for all.


**About you:**


* A tertiary qualification in fields related especially to toxicology, or to environmental public health or health and environmental sciences is highly desirable.
* Demonstrated knowledge of risks to human health from environmental hazards and expertise in risk assessment, risk communication and risk management.

**What we offer:**


* The opportunity to perform meaningful work, making direct contributions toward enabling Victorians to be the healthiest people in the world.
* A wide range of growth and development opportunities within the department and wider Victorian Public Service.
* A strong commitment to work\-life balance, including a diverse array of flexible working arrangements.


**How to apply:**


Applications should include a resume and a cover letter. Click the \`Apply' button to view further information about the role including key contact details and the advertisement closing date.


We are committed to developing and supporting a workforce that is well equipped and highly motivated to provide responsive and quality services to all Victorians. We continue to build an inclusive workplace that embraces diversity of backgrounds and differences to realise the potential of our employees for innovation and delivering services aimed at enhancing the lives of all Victorians. All roles can be worked flexibly and we encourage applications from Aboriginal people, people with disability, LGBTIQ\+ and people from culturally diverse backgrounds. Please contact us if you require any adjustments to participate in the recruitment process at inclusion@health.vic.gov.au. For more information on our commitment to inclusion and diversity see inclusion and diversity at the Department of Health.



If you have any queries in relation to participation in recruitment processes at Health, or experience any issues in applying, please feel free to email talentacquisition@health.vic.gov.au. Please note that unsolicited applications from third parties cannot be accepted. If you have questions regarding the role, please message the contact person listed on the advertisement directly.


Preferred applicants may be required to complete a police check and other pre\-employment checks. Information provided will be treated in line with our Privacy Policy.

jobs.title: Remediation Team Leader
jobs.description:
**Remediation Team Leader**
===========================

  

**Date:** 29 Sept 2026


**Location:** Sydney, Australia


**Company:** Singtel Group

  

Optus is an Australian telecommunications company, delivering more than 11 million services to our customers every day across mobile, broadband, and digital solutions.

  

As the Remediation Team Leader at Optus, you'll play a critical leadership role within our customer division. In this role, you will lead a team responsible for resolving the most complex, high\-risk, and high\-impact customer issues. You will bring strong remediation expertise and leadership capability to guide decision\-making in situations requiring advanced risk assessment, ethical judgement, and stakeholder alignment — directly influencing customer outcomes and protecting Optus’ reputation.

  

The role manages a team with independent review of escalated and complex cases, including matters referred by the ExCo, senior leaders, the Telecommunications Industry Ombudsman (TIO) and other external bodies.

  

***Please note this is a 12\-month fixed term opportunity.***

  

**What You’ll Do \| Your day to day will consist of**


* Taking full ownership of high\-risk, high\-impact customer issues, including executive complaints, tribunal matters, and privacy incidents.
* Leading a team of remediation specialists, ensuring effective triage, prioritisation, and resolution of complex cases within defined SLAs.
* Managing executive\-level complaints, balancing urgency, customer harm risk, and regulatory exposure.
* Providing clear, high\-quality recommendations and remediation outcomes to senior leaders on complex, high\-risk matters.
* Ensuring adherence to internal standards and regulatory requirements, particularly in non\-standard or exception\-based scenarios.
**What You Bring \| What makes you perfect for the role?**


* Proven experience (essential) leading teams in a customer remediation environment, with clear accountability for outcomes.
* Strong experience managing high\-risk, high\-impact remediation cases, including executive complaints, tribunal matters, and issues with regulatory and reputational implications.
* Demonstrated ability to lead decision\-making and provide governance across customer advocacy, remediation, and dispute resolution in a highly regulated environment.
* Experience overseeing vulnerable customer cases, ensuring appropriate remediation outcomes.
* Exceptional judgement and critical thinking when managing complex, sensitive issues where there is little or no precedent.
* Strong communication and stakeholder management skills, with the ability to influence senior leaders and represent the function effectively.
* Ability to interpret regulatory frameworks and align to operational practices.
**The good stuff…. \| What’s in it for you?**


* Competitive remuneration and employee discounts. Make life easier (and more affordable) with $80 monthly credit and 25% off Optus products and unique shopping discounts with our retail partners.
* Flexible working arrangements with opportunities to work three days in the office, two days remote or home.
* Vibrant and collaborative office campus that includes cafes, convenience store, chill out zones, GP, post office, gym and on\-site childcare centre.
* Competitive leave policies, including additional 'Connected’ days to focus on culture, family, health, community, or whatever’s important to you.
* We support growing families with inclusive, carer\-neutral paid Parental Leave of up to 16 weeks.
* Build meaningful connections through employee\-led networks and diversity initiatives including Culture Connect, Elevate Women, Disability Network and Express Yourself (LGBTQIA\+).
* Put your wellbeing first with free access to counselling and support services, 24/7 — in\-person, by phone, SMS, or video.
* Free Optus bus from Macquarie University Metro Station (every 6\-8 minutes); morning and afternoon.
At Optus, we are strengthened by others and that means valuing diversity and saying ‘yes’ to embracing individual differences. We are committed to ensuring that our application process provides an equal employment opportunity to all job seekers, including individuals from diverse gender, cultural and linguistic backgrounds, individuals with a disability, individuals identifying as being part of the LGBTQIA\+ community, individuals who may have served in the armed forces or who identify as Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander. We also want to do our best to make our recruitment process inclusive. If you require any adjustments or accessibility support to participate fairly and equitably in the recruitment process, please email AccessibleRecruitment@optus.com.au or call 1800 309 170\.

  

For more information on Diversity, Inclusion \& Belonging at Optus, please visit https://www.optus.com.au/about/inclusion\-diversity
